title: Chemistry-infused bandit framework for interpretable autonomous campaign of electrocatalysis
authors: Yi-An Lai; Muxin Xiong; Jingwen Sun; Aijian Huang; Max Van Fleet; Hongyuan Sheng; J A Kim; Felisha Kuo; Tai Ying Lai; Xuian-Rou Lin; Yuehua Chen; Weitong Zhang; Hao Ming Chen; Chong Liu
abstract: Abstract Autonomous experimentation offers a time-efficient route towards accelerated catalyst discovery, but current practices often rely on black-box models that are difficult to interpret. Here we demonstrate the paradigm of interpretable autonomous exploration of a 12-dimensional space in the electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction by integrating an interpretable decision-making artificial intelligence with a fully automated electrochemical platform. Guided by a human’s chemistry-informed hypothesis, a chemistry-infused bandit is established to reflect the locally quadratic approximation between synthetic conditions and electrocatalytic activities near the explored optimum region. Not only does such a decision-making bandit lead to the discovery of previously unreported, earth-abundant electrocatalysts at least comparable to Pt-based ones, the bandit also reveals model-derived hypothesis for how synthetic conditions affect the electrocatalysts’ performance near the identified local optima as autonomous inquiry proceeds, which is otherwise untenable from black-box ones. Incorporating chemistry-informed hypothesis into the decision-making bandit is generally applicable to any chemistry problem and offers a framework for autonomous investigation, advancing hypothesis generation for catalyst’s design principles beyond simple optimization.

title: Bioinspired ventral-groove fibers for volume-programmable pneumatic actuation
authors: Xiaoyu Zhang; Qianyi Li; Xiaolong Li; Ziang Li; Haoran Qiu; Shiyun Qian; Ying Yi Tan; Hong Yee Low; Tural Khudiyev
abstract: Pneumatic actuation plays a central role in soft robotics, with conventional systems relying on pressure-driven chamber deformation and closed-loop feedback for precise control. Here, we introduce bioinspired ventral-groove filamentary fibers that reframe pneumatic actuation from pressure-dominated chambers to volume-programmable fiber architectures, enabling previously unexplored robotic capabilities. Coupling microgroove unfolding with elastic expansion, these molecularly programmed fibers achieve reversible 400× area expansion at ultralow pressure (∼0.8 kPa) and scale from ∼100 μm to centimeter-scale diameters and tens of meters in length, supporting micro- to macro-scale robotic systems. We demonstrate responsive textile actuation through an everyday flotation garment with 20-m fibers seamlessly integrated into clothing. We also show a gripping approach with three capabilities: disturbance-robust high-precision grasping, conformal handling of fragile nerve-like filaments and delicate incense-ash cones, and open-loop operation that reduces reliance on sensory feedback. By establishing a volume-programmable actuation paradigm, this work paves the way for low-pressure pneumatic technologies in soft robotics and responsive textiles.

title: Water in kimberlitic olivine provides insights into kimberlite ascent and diamond transport
authors: Soumendu Sarkar; Rondi M. Davies; Qiwei Zhang; Luísa D.V. Carvalho; Thomas Stachel; David Graham Pearson
abstract: Kimberlites are volatile-rich magmas that transport diamonds from the deep lithosphere to the surface, yet the exact processes controlling their variable diamond abundances remain debated. Compiled dataset of water contents in mantle olivine shows that kimberlites containing water-rich (>40 wt. ppm) olivine exhibit higher diamond grades. Diffusion modeling coupled with estimates of the ascent velocities of olivine xenocrysts indicate that preserved water in the cores of olivine crystals reflects variable magma ascent rates. High water contents are indicative of rapid ascent that not only limits hydrogen loss but also leads to enhanced diamond transport. Conversely, slower ascent promotes olivine dehydration and reduction in diamond-carrying capacity. The link between olivine water content and diamond grade highlights that ascent rate is a key factor in controlling the varied diamond abundance in kimberlites. Water in olivine thus provides an additional, complementary, and cost-effective proxy for estimating kimberlite ascent and diamond-carrying efficiency. This study links higher diamond grades in kimberlites to water-rich olivine. Modeling suggests that rapid magma ascent preserves higher olivine water contents and facilitates efficient diamond transport, highlighting ascent rate as a key control on diamond preservation.

title: Observation of inherent chiral Smith–Purcell effect via symmetry breaking
authors: Juan‐Feng Zhu; Fei Chen; Jun-Xuan Chen; Junkang Shan; Ayan Nussupbekov; Febiana Tjiptoharsono; Xuan Dong; Mu Wang; Cheng-Wei Qiu; Zhaogang Dong; Ruwen Peng; Lin Wu
abstract: The Smith–Purcell effect arises when charged particles move near a periodic structure, emitting radiation. Conventional approaches for generating chiral Smith–Purcell radiation rely on metasurface phase engineering or resonant mode interference, typically producing narrow-band, weakly chiral emission. Here, we introduce a resonance-interference-free mechanism that leverages the properties of the charged particles themselves. Using a non-chiral, non-resonant silicon grating, we demonstrate broadband, tunable Smith–Purcell radiation with high chirality, achieving a record-high degree of polarization of 0.87. This is enabled by converting the transverse spin angular momentum of electron-induced evanescent waves into a longitudinal form, producing opposite chirality at different azimuthal angles. Beam twisting or displacement offers precise control over chirality, paving the way for compact chiral light sources, advanced X-ray imaging, and integrated particle diagnostics platforms. Existing approaches for generating chiral Smith–Purcell radiation remain limited. Here, the authors overcome these limitations by uncovering the inherent chirality of the Smith–Purcell effect using non-chiral, non-resonant silicon gratings. By controlling the electron–grating configuration, this chirality can be selectively manipulated to produce tunable and highly chiral polarized radiation.

title: Non-polar surface passivation of PbS Quantum Dots using metal thiolates enables photodiodes rivaling InGaAs performance
authors: Debranjan Mandal; Yongjie Wang; Carmelita Rodà; Miguel Dosil; Gaurav Kumar; Lucheng Peng; Gerasimos Konstantatos
abstract: Abstract Colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) short-wave infrared (SWIR) detectors (1-2 µm) are of great interest for a plethora of applications including autonomous driving, machine vision, night and adverse weather imaging, in view of their low-cost and compatibility to read-out electronics. However, to date, CQDs photodetectors still suffer from high dark current and thereby noise such that their performance remains inferior to epitaxially grown III-V semiconductors. This performance gap originates from the limited passivation of non-polar surfaces existent in large PbS CQDs needed to access the SWIR spectral range. Here we report on a lead-thiolate based chemistry that serves to passivate both polar and non-polar surfaces of PbS CQDs yielding inks with unprecedented optoelectronic quality evidenced by open circuit voltage deficit and dark current activation energies matching those of single crystalline semiconductors. As a result, we demonstrate infrared photodetectors with remarkable thermal resilience, very low dark current density ( ~ 34 nA cm −2 at −1 V) and a specific detectivity D* of ~8×10 12 Jones. The measured D* value is on par with that of commercially available InGaAs photodiodes (PDs).

title: Heatwave-induced capacity bottlenecks in European electricity grids
authors: Enming Liang; Minghua Chen; Srinivasan Keshav
abstract: Abstract Heatwaves are becoming more frequent, intense and prolonged as the climate warms, placing stress on the electricity infrastructure underpinning modern societies. Yet how rising temperatures erode grid capacity remains under-quantified. Existing power-flow models either oversimplify thermal effects or become computationally intractable when resolving them in detail. Here we introduce a unified, computationally efficient framework that jointly captures temperature-dependent demand, generator derating and spatially resolved transmission-line thermal limits within an alternating-current optimal power-flow formulation. Applying it to the Western European system with open-access grid, high-resolution weather reanalysis and demand data, we simulate hundreds of projected heatwave scenarios for 2026–2030. Across these represented grid configurations, the analysis reveals substantial national disparities: the Spanish grid exhibits temperature-induced bottlenecks and load shedding, whereas the German grid remains comparatively resilient. Heatwave-aware power-flow analysis thus uncovers structural bottlenecks and should be integrated into grid planning and adaptation as heatwaves intensify under climate change.

title: Evaluation of SWOT HR PIXC version D water level time series of small lakes
authors: Simon Jakob Köhn; Karina Nielsen
abstract: Abstract. Satellite altimetry has successfully monitored inland waters for more than 30 years and is increasingly important as the demand for freshwater grows and climate change accelerates. Launched in December 2022, the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite is the first to provide 2D spatially distributed elevation measurements, with a 21-day revisit time and better coverage depending on latitude and a nominal requirement to detect lakes as small as 0.06 km2. Here, we evaluate the SWOT L2 HR PIXC version D data product (if available at the time of writing) to construct time series of water surface elevation (WSE) and capture their relative WSE change in 37 Danish lakes with a surface area between 0.25 km2 and 40 km2 via the summary measures RMSE and Pearson’s correlation coefficient (PCC). We tested six selection criteria to aggregate one WSE value per lake and timestamp. The median unbiased RMSE of SWOT vs gauge is 5.34 cm, and the median PCC is 0.91. We find indications that SWOT’s PIXC data contains time–varying residual roll–errors over Danish lakes. We demonstrate that our approach performs slightly better than filtered SWOT L2 HR LakeSP prior data from Hydrocron in terms of RMSE and PCC (6.05 cm and 0.89), while retaining roughly double the number of valid timestamps over the overlapping period.

title: Determining depth-resolved spatial distribution of solid–electrolyte interphase using non-destructive angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy for lithium-metal batteries
authors: Giulio D’Acunto; Sanzeeda Baig Shuchi; Yi Cui; Stacey F. Bent
abstract: The solid electrolyte interphase is a key performance regulator in Li-metal batteries, which are regarded as an important technology for future energy storage. Understanding this crucial interphase through non-destructive analysis is essential to advance the performance and lifespan of Li-metal batteries. We introduce angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy as a non-destructive technique for the depth-profile analysis of the solid electrolyte interphase in Li-metal batteries. Importantly, we show that this characterization technique displays a distinct advantage in preserving the solid electrolyte interphase's integrity compared to traditional sputtering-based depth-profiling. Our findings add to the understanding of compositional differences in the solid electrolyte interphase before the onset of Li electrodeposition and after Li plating. Moreover, we find significant variations in the thickness and distribution of solid electrolyte interphase species across different classes of electrolytes, which strongly influence the solid electrolyte interphase's protective properties and, by extension, Li-metal battery performance. This study benchmarks the application of angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy in revealing detailed, depth-resolved chemical composition of the solid electrolyte interphase in a non-destructive approach. Understanding the solid–electrolyte interphase formed on lithium is vital for improving the lifetime of lithium metal batteries. Here, authors show that angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy can reveal the depth-dependent composition of the interfacial layer without damaging it by ion sputtering.

title: Canadian lakes show contrasting phosphorus trends across climatic regions
authors: Hongwei Guo; Jinhui Jeanne Huang‬‬‬‬; Yunlin Zhang; John P. Smol; Xiaotong Zhu; Ling Jiang; Longwei Li; Weipeng Lin; Han Zhang; Lunche Wang
abstract: Phosphorus regulates lake productivity and water quality, yet long-term changes in lake phosphorus and their climatic drivers remain poorly understood at continental scales. Here we show how total phosphorus changes across 15,240 Canadian lakes > 5 km2 from 1984 to 2025 using a deep neural network trained with 35,452 field measurements and applied to 386,727 Landsat images. Arctic tundra watersheds show increasing phosphorus concentrations of 0.15 μg/L yr−1, whereas boreal forest, temperate forest, agricultural and urban watersheds show declines of 0.07, 0.11, 0.16 and 0.12 μg/L yr−1, respectively. Path analyses link northern increases to ground warming and soil erosion, consistent with permafrost-related phosphorus mobilization. Southern declines are associated with vegetation greening, hydrological change, and reduced human phosphorus inputs, while surface runoff remains important in agricultural and urban systems. These findings reveal contrasting climate-sensitive phosphorus trajectories and show that climate change can reinforce or counteract nutrient management gains, highlighting the need to integrate region-specific climate adaptation into lake management. Lake phosphorus increased in Arctic Canada but declined across other climatic regions, with northern increases linked to ground warming and soil erosion, according to a study that combined field measurements with deep learning analysis of Landsat imagery from 15,240 lakes between 1984 and 2025.

title: Benchmarking convection-permitting climate simulations for hydrometeorological characterizations: a comparative study of WRF-SAAG and observation-based products in Chile
authors: Sofía Segovia; Pablo A. Mendoza; Miguel Ángel Lagos-Zúñiga; Lucía Scaff; Andreas Franz Prein
abstract: Abstract. Over the last years, significant progress has been made in the development of convection-permitting climate models (CPCMs), especially for improving precipitation modeling in regions with complex terrain. Recently, the South American Affinity Group (SAAG) developed a novel high-resolution dataset — hereafter referred to as the WRF-SAAG dataset — by dynamically downscaling the ERA5 reanalysis using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model over South America for the period 2000–2021. In this paper, we evaluate the quality of WRF-SAAG daily precipitation and temperature simulations using observations from meteorological stations over continental Chile for the period 2001–2018, and present comparisons against two gridded meteorological products – CR2MET and RF-MEP – which are based on in-situ meteorological station measurements and have been widely used for hydrometeorological applications in this region. We found that, although the precipitation products correctly replicated the percentage correct (PC) of observed events and non-events (PC ≥ 0.64), detection accuracy varied within each Chilean macrozone –defined by latitudinal bands – with worse performance in the Far North (between 17.5 – 26° S) and Patagonia (between 43.7 – 56° S) — median Critical Success Index (CSI) < 0.49 for events > 5 mm/d— compared to the central region (CSI ≥ 0.44 for events > 5 mm/d). The evaluation of daily precipitation and extreme temperatures against station observations using Tang’s Kling-Gupta efficiency (KGET) and its components reveals that all datasets performed better in reproducing precipitation in rainy regions (median KGET ≥ 0.65 in the Southern macrozone), while in arid areas such as the Near North during summer, the median KGET was negative. The CR2MET product consistently provided the best performance metrics for extreme precipitation and temperature, partly because it includes information from the stations used for evaluation. Finally, the application of the TUW hydrological model shows that WRF-SAAG simulations achieved runoff estimations comparable to the best observation-based products, with the best metrics obtained in the Southern macrozone, where the median objective function (OF) —defined as the average of KGE' and KGE' (1/q) — remains above 0.87 (0.67) during the calibration (evaluation) period. More broadly, the results presented here show that – despite some remaining challenges in arid climate regions – kilometer-scale climate models can deliver information of a quality comparable to that of observation-based products for hydrological applications in Chile.

title: A porous solid electrolyte interface enables efficient electroreduction of captured carbon to CO
authors: Shanhe Gong; Qing Xia; Yanjie Zhai; Weisong Li; Jie Wu; Yingying Zhou; Yucong Liao; Kuang Zhu; Yuchen Yang; Yile Yang; Xiaojie She; Zhaolong Wang; Huaming Li; Xiao Zhang; Shu Ping Lau
abstract: Direct electrochemical conversion of captured carbon species offers a route to avoid the energy-intensive steps of thermal CO2 release, compression and transport in conventional carbon capture and utilization. In proton exchange membrane (PEM) reactors, however, the acidic cathode environment promotes hydrogen evolution and limits CO2 regeneration from (bi)carbonate capture media, resulting in low carbon utilization and high energy demand. Here we show a modular PEM–porous solid electrolyte (PSE) reactor for direct conversion of (bi)carbonate to CO. Using a transparent cell with in situ visualization, we reveal that the PSE regulates proton transport, reduces local proton reduction, limits bubble accumulation and facilitates CO2 transport to the cathode. The PEM–PSE reactor achieves a CO Faradaic efficiency of 90% at 200 mA cm−2, a carbon efficiency of 84%, and an energy consumption of ~26.0 GJ t−1 CO. It operates at current densities up to 800 mA cm−2, reaching a CO rate of ~8.0 mmol h−1 cm−2. These results highlight the regulation of proton and gas transport in the electrochemical conversion of captured carbon. Turning captured carbon dioxide into useful chemicals can save energy, but combining capture and conversion is difficult. Here, the authors report a membrane reactor converts bicarbonate solutions directly into carbon monoxide with high carbon efficiency and lower energy use.

title: Ultrasonic metamaterial at MHz frequencies using microstructured glass
authors: Oscar Demeulenaere; Nikita Ustimenko; Athanasios G. Athanassiadis; Lovish Gulati; Carsten Rockstuhl; Peer Fischer
abstract: Acoustic metamaterials enhance traditional material properties, providing opportunities to shape sound fields in applications ranging from biomedical imaging and clinical therapy to nondestructive testing. However, at the megahertz frequency range, only a few metamaterial architectures exist. They are often highly attenuating or difficult to manufacture and generally provide limited control. Here, we introduce a megahertz-frequency ultrasonic metamaterial based on laser-engraved glass. By structuring metavoxels with different engraving patterns, we define an anisotropic metamaterial exhibiting local variations in the sound speed of up to 20% compared to unstructured glass and losses 100× lower than in comparable three-dimensional-printed metamaterials. We use this metamaterial to define a library of standard elements that can be modularly combined to shape complex-patterned ultrasonic fields. Our experiments are supported by a theoretical model, which provides additional insights into the microstructural origin of the metamaterial behavior and opens the door to designing tailored ultrasound fields and responses.

title: Strain-engineered fabrication of high-density aligned graphene-based nanoscrolls via UV-tunable adhesive tapes
authors: Maki Nakatani; Akari Sudo; Pablo Solís‐Fernández; Haiming Sun; Satoru Fukamachi; Tomoki MAEZAWA; Tatsuya Ikuta; Takako Matsunaga; Aika Uchida; Masatoshi Mitsuhara; Yung-Chang Lin; Koji Takahashi; Rika Matsumoto; Kazu Suenaga; Takahiro Yamamoto
abstract: Abstract Graphene nanoscrolls (GNSs), one-dimensional nanostructures formed by rolling up a single sheet of graphene, exhibit electronic and mechanical properties distinct from the original graphene sheet. Although several methods have been proposed to synthesize GNSs, achieving high-density GNSs with controlled scroll chirality and direction remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the strain-engineered fabrication of large-scale GNSs using an ultraviolet (UV) light-tunable adhesive tape. The UV tape is stretched to apply tensile strain to graphene stacked on it, and releasing the applied strain by detaching the graphene from the tape results in the formation of GNSs. This strain-assisted method gives isolated GNSs of increased density ( ≈ 380 nanoscrolls per mm) and length (90 μm). This method also allows control of the scroll angle, i.e., chiral angle, by controlling the stretch direction of the tape/graphene stack. The nanoscroll structure allows the intercalation of metal chloride molecules, resulting in an increase of the electrical conductivity. Furthermore, heteronanoscrolls of graphene and MoS 2 are realized by stretching MoS 2 /graphene heterostacks, exhibiting clear optical response. Our controlled synthesis of GNSs and heteronanoscrolls provides an opportunity to manipulate nanomaterials through the strain engineering with the functional UV tape.

title: Stable coexistence and transport of lytic phage infections with migrating bacterial hosts
authors: Jacopo Marchi; Chadiga Khalek; Abir George; Joshua S. Weitz; Remy Chait
abstract: Bacteriophages (phages), viruses that exclusively infect bacteria, coexist with their bacterial hosts across diverse environments at densities exceeding 10 7 per milliliter in marine surface waters, 10 8 per milliliter in soils, and 10 9 per milliliter in the human gut. In contrast, phage lysis of bacterial populations within well-mixed in vitro environments select for the emergence of phage-resistant bacterial mutants, which, in turn, select for host-range expansion phage mutants and, typically, the collapse of phage populations altogether. This gap in outcome raises a question: What enables long-term phage-bacteria coexistence? Here, we show how interactions in space can facilitate stable coexistence and long-range transport of virulent phage along with migrating bacteria. Combining theory, simulation, and experiments across multiple phage-bacteria systems, we reveal a chemotaxis-driven mechanism that robustly stabilizes coexistence and dispersal of virulent phages with migrating hosts. These findings suggest the ecological relevance of spatial interaction mechanisms that reinforce stability between antagonistic partners in the absence of perpetual cycles of defense and counterdefense, which may be broadly applicable across phage-bacteria systems.

title: Scentronic: An artificial intelligence–assisted olfactory interface for remote odor sharing and transmission
authors: Chunyu Yang; Qi Wang; Chen Wang; Antonia Akoto-Yeboah; Shaoru Cheng; Billings Amoah; Yizhen Jia; Shulin Chen; Akhil Canumalla; Kai Zhao; Christopher T. Simons; Jinghua Li
abstract: Recent years have witnessed the surge of human-machine interfaces (HMIs) for various applications. Olfaction is a fundamental chemical sense crucial to perception, memory, and emotion. Current limitations arise from the difficulty of accurately capturing, transmitting, and reproducing odor signals, and the lack of standardized, network-enabled platforms. This work presents an internet of things (IoT)-enabled olfactory interface for remote odor sensing and stimulation. The system integrates an artificial intelligence-assisted odor sensing platform with a wearable piezoelectric olfactory actuation system. We demonstrate the design, characterization, and application of this framework, which integrates devices, circuit architecture, and software algorithms. Applications in medical contexts include psychophysical testing to study olfactory pathways and evaluate sensory loss. We further showcase multisensory stimulation through integrated olfactory and gustatory interfaces for enhanced immersion. This study establishes a scalable framework for IoT-based olfactory interaction, advancing HMIs toward a future that includes the long-overlooked chemical senses.

title: Regionalized greenhouse gas emissions and infrastructure requirements for future global iron and steel production
authors: Tom Terlouw; Carina Harpprecht; Christian Bauer
abstract: Abstract The steel industry accounts for approximately 7–9% of global greenhouse gas emissions, making it a key sector for decarbonization. Here, we quantify current and prospective greenhouse gas emissions from crude steel production facilities worldwide. Based on life cycle assessment, current greenhouse gas emissions of global crude steel production are around 3.7 gigatonnes carbon dioxide equivalent per year, highly concentrated in Asia. Depending on the future 2 ◦ C scenario in 2040, greenhouse gas emissions may decline by up to 70%, to 1.1–2.3 gigatonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent per year. Also, we show that decarbonizing steel may require up to 90 million tonnes of hydrogen per year, 1.0 gigatonne of carbon dioxide storage per year, and/or electricity supply with up to 6,000 terawatt-hours per year, more than twice the European Union’s current electricity supply. Our results highlight the importance of regional context and the substantial infrastructure needs of low-carbon steel production.

title: Kinetic acceleration of phosphate remediation in dilute aquatic environments via photovoltaic-driven solid-state electrolyte electrocoagulation
authors: Shan Liu; Xiaosong Gu; Zhongxin Chen; Jiaxiang Liang; Hong Chen
abstract: The kinetic limitations of reclaiming low-level orthophosphate (PO43−) in low-conductivity natural water bodies impede the in-depth remediation of anthropogenic eutrophication. Conventional adsorption and electrocoagulation (EC) methods are hindered by excessive chemical reagent consumption, high electrical energy demand, and substantial metal electrode consumption. Here, we present a solid-state electrolyte electrocoagulation (SEE) system that employs an interfacial coupling strategy to integrate dynamic ion enrichment with in situ anodic coagulation. By concentrating PO43− at the solid-state electrolyte interface, the system overcomes inherent mass-transport constraints and enhances ion conductivity in dilute media. This localized concentration gradient accelerates apparent reaction kinetics, achieving a removal rate of 0.197 mg/L·min, minimizing energy consumption to 0.0325 kWh/g P and iron consumption to 3.829 g/g P. Consequently, SEE enables efficient, one-step purification below strict regulatory thresholds ( ≤ 0.02 mg/L, China’s Class I Surface Water Environmental Quality Standard). Validated as a photovoltaic-integrated, boat-mounted unit, this approach offers a robust decentralized solution for natural waters, with techno-economic and life cycle assessments confirming its economic viability and low environmental footprint. A solar-powered electrocoagulation system rapidly removes low-level phosphate from natural waters via interfacial ion concentration, overcoming mass-transfer limits for efficient decentralized water purification with low energy and material use.

title: How high-pressure ices on large ocean worlds can support habitability: The compatibility of amino acids into ice VI and VII
authors: Jihua Hao; Can Liu; Feixiang Liu; Chengtao Zhang; Javed Akhter Mondal; Christopher R. Glein; Hervé Cardon; Gilles Montagnac; Xiaobin Cao; I. M. Daniel
abstract: Water oceans in large icy moons and exoplanets are isolated from the rocky interior by thick layers of high-pressure ice, which hinder the direct release of nutrients and organics derived from water-rock interaction to the ocean. Possible uptake of these bio-essential compounds into high-pressure ice phases could regulate their availability in the ocean, but this process is poorly constrained. Here, we measured partition coefficients of glycine and alanine into ices VI and VII under elevated temperature-pressure conditions using a diamond-anvil cell. We observed moderate compatibility of glycine and alanine with partition coefficients: K p ,glycine = 0.14 and 0.40 in ices VI and VII, respectively; K p ,alanine = 0.21 and 0.35 in ices VI and VII, respectively. First-principles calculations suggested that amino acids could be incorporated into high-pressure ice’s lattice via cogrowth. Compatibility of amino acids into high-pressure ices would favor their transport in large extraterrestrial oceans, opening an avenue to habitability.

title: High ambipolar mobility fluorinated MXene for ultrasensitive biosensing transistors
authors: Yang Yue; Junhong Zhao; Xuejun Wang; Yanan Tang; Yunqi Liu; Dacheng Wei
abstract: Transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes) are emerging as transformative materials for bioelectronics. However, the advancement of MXene-based field-effect transistor (FET) biosensors is hindered by the lack of high-quality aqueous-stable materials and the low signal transduction efficiency intrinsic to their metallic nature. To address these issues, we report an ultrasensitive biosensing platform enabled by an in-situ fluorination strategy of MXene. By substituting unstable oxygen-containing terminations with chemically stable fluorine terminations in a mild reaction, we synthesized high-quality fluorinated MXene with the record-breaking ambipolar field-effect mobility (μ p = 10.42 cm 2 V −1 s −1 , μ n = 30.23 cm 2 V −1 s −1 ). The highly electronegative fluorinated interface suppresses interfacial electrical double-layer capacitance, boosting signal transduction efficiency. Consequently, the platform achieves the lowest limit of detection (LOD) of 0.26 fg ml −1 for Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigen MPT64 among MXene FETs up to date, accompanied by a high current response of 35.02% at LOD. Clinical validation across 126 serum samples demonstrated a diagnostic accuracy of 97.6% with a detection time of 38 s, exhibiting the high-performance and reliable biosensing in complex physiological environments.

title: Free tropospheric halogen oxidation drives mercury deposition in the Asia Pacific region
authors: Ju Hyeon Lee; Young-Gwang Kim; Ho‐In Lee; Seung Hyeon Lim; Joël Savarino; Alfonso Saiz‐Lopez; Jeroen E. Sonke; Kitae Kim; Ki‐Tae Park; Eunho Jang; Yeongcheol Han; Aryeh I. Feinberg; Hélène Angot; Ilann Bourgeois; Sae Yun Kwon
abstract: Asian outflow represents 50% of global anthropogenic mercury emissions, but the atmospheric oxidation pathways controlling its deposition to the adjacent Pacific Ocean remain poorly constrained. Using multi-year snow and atmospheric mercury isotope measurements from Mt. Halla, Jeju Island, Korea, we delineate the mercury sources and oxidation pathways governing deposition to marginal Asia and the western Pacific. Mass-independent fractionation of even-number mercury isotopes (even-MIF; Δ 200 Hg) correlates with both air mass transport distance and trajectory altitude, indicating the importance of free tropospheric mercury photo-oxidation triggering even-MIF. Coupled anomalies between Δ 200 Hg and oxygen isotopes of nitrate (Δ 17 O(NO 3 - )) in snow indicate that reactive bromine, generated from debromination of local sea salt aerosol, sustains oxidative capacity in the free troposphere and drives active mercury deposition to Mt. Halla snow. Isotope mixing models quantify that halogen-mediated free tropospheric mercury oxidation (68%) exceeds near-surface oxidation (32%). Our results provide field-based evidence for a bromine-driven free tropospheric photo-oxidation mechanism regulating mercury deposition to Asia-Pacific ecosystems.

title: All-soft organic electrochemical diodes based on asymmetric active layers for signal isolation in deformable electronics
authors: Sehyun Kim; Minji Kim; Haechan Park; Kihyun Sim; J. I. Jang; Yerin Kim; Jinyeong Park; Donghyung Shin; Myeonghyeon Na; Kyoseung Sim
abstract: All-soft electronics have emerged as a promising platform for deformable and human-centric systems, yet the development of mechanically compliant diodes remains a major challenge due to limitations in material compatibility, device architecture, and stable operation under deformation. Electrochemical approaches offer a viable route to address this challenge by enabling bulk, low-voltage charge modulation in soft materials without relying on rigid junction interfaces. Here, we report, to the best of our knowledge, the first all-soft organic electrochemical diode (OECD) based on an asymmetric active-layer geometry. The device incorporates a transfer-printed ultrathin ion-gel interface that preserves conformal coverage and the active electrochemical architecture under strain. The device achieves high rectification through polarity-dependent electrochemical potential redistribution, with a rectification ratio of up to 2.23 × 10 4 at ±1 V and stable operation under tensile strains of up to 30% and repeated mechanical deformation. This ion-gel-based architecture preserves the electrochemical asymmetry required for diode operation while maintaining structural integrity under strain. Beyond the individual device, the all-soft OECD enables deformable rectifiers and logic gates and functions as a key signal-isolation element that suppresses cross-talk in a deformable pressure-sensing array. These results establish an electrochemical diode platform that combines mechanical deformability, high rectification performance, and circuit-level compatibility, providing a pathway toward fully deformable and integrated human-centric electronic systems.

title: Identification and genetic characterization of megabase-scale plasmids of Enterobacteriaceae
authors: Allison K. Guitor; Shuai Wang; Owen T. Tuck; Brian Firek; Nadezda Kryuchkova-Mostacci; April A. Jauhal; Lin-Xing Chen; Agata H Dziegiel; Stephen G. Baker; Vu Thuy Duong; Alison E. Mather; Jukka Corander; Anu Kantele; Liat Shenhav; Markus Hilty
abstract: Abstract Humans and animals are ubiquitously colonized by Enterobacteriaceae , including both commensals and clinically significant pathogens. Here, we report 21 complete Enterobacteriaceae megaplasmid genomes of up to 1.58 Mbp in length spanning two major clades that are highly divergent from previously described plasmids. Of these, three were reconstructed from isolates of Escherichia coli and Shigella flexneri ; others were potentially hosted by species of Citrobacter and Enterobacter . Related megabase-scale plasmids were detected in at least 400 infant and adult gut, and other microbiomes. Diverse Enterobacteriaceae hosts, conjugation machinery, and DNA modification patterns suggest that these elements are self-transmissible, with a broad host range. The plasmids encode multi-drug efflux systems and potential secreted effectors. Up to 208 tRNAs are encoded and include sequence variants that may counter tRNA-centric defense mechanisms. Overall, the vast plasmid coding capacity may broaden host range, increase competitiveness, control invasion by other elements, and counter programmed cell death.

title: Divergent anaerobic fates of biodegradable plastics in landfill leachate
authors: Shinhyeong Choe; Hyungmin Choi; Hoseong Moon; Woohyuk Shin; Sunho Park; 박희주; Ju Yong Lee; Sukhwan Yoon; Konstantinos T. Konstantinidis; Changsoo Lee; Jaewook Myung
abstract: Biodegradable plastics (BPs) are increasingly promoted as sustainable alternatives to conventional polymers, yet their fate in landfills remains poorly understood. Here, we evaluated the anaerobic biodegradability of three BPs, polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), poly(lactic acid) (PLA), and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT), in landfill leachate under mesophilic conditions by quantifying carbon conversion to biogas. The BPs exhibited sharply contrasting degradation trajectories: PHB mineralized completely within 17 d, whereas PLA underwent substantial mineralization over 320 d (83.6%), extending beyond the well-established expectation of limited mesophilic degradation. In contrast, PBAT remained largely recalcitrant. Multi-omics analyses linked PHB and PLA depolymerization to the biofilm–polymer interface, with depolymerase transcription tracking their distinct degradation phases. Putative depolymerase homologs were widespread across recovered bacterial genomes, yet only a subset showed transcriptional support. This active fraction included multiple under-characterized lineages outside the taxonomic range of experimentally validated degrader genomes, revealing a marked disconnect between genomic potential and realized activity. Our findings show that anaerobic biodegradation outcomes in landfill leachate cannot be inferred from biodegradability labels or genomic potential alone, but emerge from polymer-specific depolymerization constraints and depolymerase transcription enriched at the biofilm–polymer interface. How different biodegradable plastics break down within landfills, particularly landfill leachate, remain unclear. Here, they evaluated the anaerobic biodegradability of three BPs, polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), poly(lactic acid) (PLA), and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT), using a combination of genome-resolved multi-omics.

title: Balancing the Performance Trade-off of Polymer Blends with Heterogeneously Dispersed Nanodomains via Reactive Processing
authors: Hengti Wang; Chao-Jie Li; Ning He; Toshikazu Miyoshi; Yongjin Li
abstract: Polymer blends are ubiquitous though there are persistent material-property trade-offs, due to the limitation of structural design. Here we report a reactive processing strategy that creates heterogeneously dispersed nano-domains (hDNs) of rubbery ethylene-acrylic ester-glycidyl methacrylate terpolymer (EGMA) in polyoxymethylene (POM) matrix. Pre-reactive blending of EGMA with poly (L-lactide) (PLLA) and subsequent melt processing with POM result in formation of the unique morphology, where PLLA serving as the leveraging forces for opposing uniform distribution via chemical bonds and macro-phase separation by physical associations. The resulting materials exhibited optimized mechanical performance impossible to be acquired with conventional counterparts. This work identifies herein innovates how reactive processing can regulate phase morphology while balancing the trade-off among toughness, ductility, strength and stiffness in multicomponent polymer blends, representing a paradigm shift in narrowing gap between structure and tailor-made property towards pilot plant scale. Polymer blends are ubiquitous though there are persistent material-property trade-offs, due to structural design. Here the authors design multicomponent polymers optimizing the material properties.

title: Transforming electrified railway into mechanical energy storage for electricity system decarbonization
authors: Can Wan; Xitong Mu; Zihan He; Hui Liu; Pierre Pinson; Ping Ju; Qianwen Xu
abstract: Abstract Decarbonizing electricity requires vast energy storage capacity worldwide, but constructing dedicated storage assets creates substantial capital, material and embodied carbon burdens. Electrified railways already exchange energy with electricity systems through traction and regenerative braking, but their inherent potential as mechanical energy storage remains unexploited. Here we show that modulation of train operations can transform electrified railways into Electrified Rail-Based Energy Storage. By analyzing 326,034 inter-stop train operations, we estimate its global potential at 190 gigawatts in 2025 and 315–579 gigawatts by 2050. Capacity expansion models for China, Europe and India indicate that it can reduce investment in conventional storage by 11.9–20.0%, corresponding to an extrapolated global value of US$14.9–35.1 billion annually. Without increasing total system cost, electricity systems with this flexible resource could further reduce operational CO 2 emissions by 94.3–258.9 million tonnes per year. Electrified railways can therefore complement conventional storage technologies for electricity system decarbonization.

title: Towards scalable DNA data storage with DNA-SaM codec system
authors: Yu Wang; Jiaxin Xu; Yang Wang; Ziang Nie; Jiaquan Huang; Mingen Li; Yaxin Wu; Yixuan Sun; Shanze Chen; Hui Mei; Zhiwei Qin; Junbiao Dai; Xiaoluo Huang
abstract: The exponential growth of global data volume is driving an urgent need for novel storage medium. Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA), nature’s genetic repository, presents a transformative solution with data storage density and lifespan orders of magnitude higher than conventional media. However, scaling DNA storage has been hindered by the complexity of codec algorithms, the generation of biochemically problematic sequences, and the absence of robust architecture for large-scale data. We present DNA-SaM, a system integrating highly efficient encoding, stringent biochemical constraint checks, and a storage unit distribution paradigm facilitated by a two-tiered indexing architecture. DNA-SaM demonstrates linear encoding time complexity and substantially reduced encoding time compared with representative approaches by in silico analysis. Critically, it proactively excludes sequences such as homopolymer runs, tandem repeats, and potential promoter motifs that could interfere with downstream biochemical processes, showing improved compatibility with in vitro and in vivo applications. It is further validated by practical data storage both in vitro and in vivo with a 100% success rate. On the basis of its encoding scheme and sequence design space, DNA-SaM could theoretically store data exceeding 270 petabytes (PB), marking an advancement in the scalability of DNA-based data storage. Scaling DNA storage is limited by complex codecs, biochemically problematic sequences, and insufficient architecture for large-scale data. Here, the authors present DNA-SaM, integrating efficient encoding, biochemical checks, and a storage unit distribution with a two-tiered indexing architecture.

title: Resolving short-term meteorological variability amplifies projected glacier loss and sea-level rise
authors: Lander Van Tricht; Matthias Huss; Harry Zekollari; Rodrigo Aguayo; Janosch Beer; Marit van Tiel; Alexandra von der Esch; Daniel Farinotti
abstract: Global glacier models typically rely on temperature-index mass balance calculations forced with aggregated meteorological data, limiting their ability to resolve short-term variability. Here, we develop a daily-resolution version of the Global Glacier Evolution Model (GloGEM), which we apply globally and compare against the monthly configuration. Our results show that the daily model more closely reproduces mass balance observations and provides a more detailed representation of glacier runoff. Accounting for short-term meteorological variability leads to systematically greater projected mass loss, with up to 25% greater loss in Svalbard. These differences arise from extreme melt days, precipitation-phase transitions, and surface-type feedbacks not fully represented at monthly resolution. Globally, the daily model yields ice volume losses of 26 ± 10% under low-emission and 47 ± 17% under high-emission scenarios over 2025-2100 (ensemble mean ± 1 StD), resulting in an additional 5-10% mass loss (20-33 mm of global mean sea-level rise) relative to the monthly implementation. Resolving high-frequency forcing, or accounting for its effects through parameterisations, is therefore essential for robust glacier projections, while its omission may systematically underestimate future glacier loss.

title: Polymer-agnostic crosslinking enables robust high-temperature dielectrics for energy storage
authors: Lu Fan; 강효민; Zongliang Xie; Xi Chen; He Li; Shiqi Lai; Ashlin M. Deatherage; Tiffany Chen; Sherrie Qian; Tao Han; Steve W. Shelton; Eric A. Dailing; Myeongjae Lee; Yalin Wang; Jinhui Tao
abstract: Capacitive energy storage under high operating temperatures and electric fields exceeds the limits of most commercial polymers. While crosslinking can, in principle, enhance electro-thermal stability of polymers, conventional approaches remain severely constrained by their reliance on polymer-specific chemistries and often introduce defects that compromise insulation. Herein we present a polymer-agnostic crosslinking platform based on nitrene-mediated C–H insertion, enabling substantial performance and stability improvement across chemically diverse commercial dielectric polymers. Using polyetherimide as a benchmark, the crosslinked film delivers a discharged energy density of 6.0 J cm−3 with >90% efficiency at 200 °C, along with robust cycling stability ( > 1 × 105 cycles) under harsh operational conditions (at 500 MV m−1) and a projected service lifetime of 60 years under standard industrial fields. This work establishes a facile and practical pathway to upgrade existing industrial polymers for reliable operation under harsh environments. In capacitive energy storage systems, crosslinking can improve polymer electrothermal stability, but conventional approaches rely on polymer-specific chemistries and often introduce defects that compromise insulating performance. Here the authors present a polymer-agnostic crosslinking platform based on nitrene mediated C–H insertion that improves performance and stability across a wide range of commercial dielectric polymers.

title: Human targeting of morphologically unique fishes amplifies the risk of functional erosion
authors: P. Bouchet; Sébastien Brosse; Aurèle Toussaint
abstract: Human societies are drawing on wild species for food, fuel, medicines, and recreation. Yet, it remains unclear whether different types of human use target species with common or unique ecological roles. Here we show that humans use a fourth (26%) of the freshwater fish species and these species occupy almost half (45.2%) of the global spectrum of fish morphological diversity. Yet, used species harbour unique trait combinations, that differ according to the way humans use the species such as fisheries, aquaculture, game fish and aquarium. Moreover, the species targeted by humans are characterised by traits that are predominantly associated with threatened species. By simulating the extinction of threatened species used by humans, we revealed a pronounced and non-random erosion of the morphological spectrum. Understanding the trait-based impacts of human use is thus essential to buffer human impact on natural resources. Conservation should therefore safeguard threatened species but also preserve irreplaceable trait combinations that support unique ecological strategies. A quarter of the world’s freshwater fish species are used for food, recreation, or ornamental purposes. These species harbour unique morphologies, many threatened, whose loss would erode irreplaceable ecological strategies.

title: Global patterns of reservoir normal water storage capacities estimated by statistical and machine learning models
authors: Ping Liu; Li Tang; XiaoHui Sun
abstract: Reservoir water storages are increasingly recognized as important tools for adapting to water-related hazards under climate change, particularly through their normal water storage (NWS). However, a critical data gap on regarding global reservoir NWS hinders our understanding of their spatial patterns and impacts on water management. This study aims to bridge this data gap by estimating the NWS for 7,250 global reservoirs using an ensemble approach that includes linear regression, machine learning, and satellite-based methods. We train and evaluate these models based on a representative sample of 801 reservoirs with reported NWS data and multiple static attributes. Among the evaluated methods, the Gradient Boosted Decision Trees model utilizing various reservoir features performed best (achieving a coefficient of determination of 0.95 and a mean absolute percentage error of 12%), and was subsequently selected to estimate the NWS for unrecorded reservoirs. Our analysis of the global reservoir NWS ratio (NWSR) at individual, basin, and national scales reveals significant spatial variations, with a global mean NWSR of 72%. The distribution of NWSRs varies considerably across different reservoir groups categorized by physical size, primary purpose, and climatic region. At the national and basin scales, the USA, Canada, China, Russia, and Brazil, along with the Yenisey, Nile, Mississippi, Parana, and Yangtze basins, account for substantial portions of the global NWS capacity. The developed dataset and the analyzed spatial patterns provide vital empirical inputs for water resource management, large-scale hydrological modeling, and climate change adaptation, ultimately supporting effective planning for sustainable freshwater supplies.

title: Functional diversity complements taxonomical diversity in productivity-biodiversity relationships in freshwaters
authors: Guohao Liu; Caio Graco‐Roza; Wenfei Liao; Ramiro Martín‐Devasa; Laura Castañeda‐Gómez; Anette Teittinen; Xinxin Qi; Yuying Li; Xiaodong Qu; Mikołaj Kokociński; Naicheng Wu; Janne Soininen
abstract: Abstract Productivity is widely considered a key driver of biodiversity, yet whether taxonomic and functional diversity respond similarly to productivity gradients remains unclear. Using phosphorus as an indicator for productivity gradient, we compiled 78 freshwater datasets spanning > 30,000 sites globally to test how productivity–biodiversity relationships (PBRs) vary across diversity dimensions, trophic groups, and ecosystems. We show that PBRs are predominantly unimodal across taxonomic and functional dimensions, with slightly weaker curvature for functional diversity. Unimodal PBRs are more pronounced in producers than in consumers and show stronger curvature in lakes than in rivers. Functional reorganization also varies along the phosphorus gradient, with the clearest contraction in resource-related trait space and marked shifts in community functional centroids. Climatic, geographic and human land-use gradients further modify PBR shape. These findings indicate that predicting biodiversity responses to productivity benefits from considering functional diversity, ecological context, and broad-scale environmental gradients.

title: Catalytic reactive-hydrogen membranes for rapid capture and hydrodefluorination of six PFAS of regulatory concern
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
authors: Min Long; Ai-Shi Wang; Welman Curi Elias; Chen Zhou; Thomas Patrick Senftle; Michael S. Wong; Jie Cheng; Bruce E. Rittmann
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) persist in aquatic environments due to their ultrastable C–F bonds and poor susceptibility to conventional treatment. Here, we report an H 2 -based catalytic-film membrane that enables PFAS destruction in ambient conditions by generating highly reactive surface (H ads * ) and subsurface hydrogen (H sub * ), the latter stored as β-phase palladium hydride (β-PdHx). Solid-state analyses evidenced β-PdHx formation and related lattice expansion with elevated H 2 chemical potential, revealing a structural mechanism that links hydrogen storage to catalytic defluorination. Mechanistically, the two hydrogen species play complementary roles: H ads * -rich Pd 0 surface enabled PFAS capture through parallel adsorption to maximize interfacial contact with active H, whereas sustained H sub * supplied the energetic driving force for stepwise hydrodefluorination consistent with sequential C–F scission. As a result, across six PFAS of regulatory concern—PFOA, PFOS, PFNA, PFHxS, PFBS, and GenX—the catalytic membrane converted all contaminants toward fully defluorinated products. Long-chain PFAS were removed and defluorinated more rapidly than short-chain analogs, while GenX showed greater recalcitrance due to its ether linkage, weaker adsorption, and higher average C–F bond dissociation energy; nonetheless, GenX still exhibited removal and defluorination, with the production of 2-propoxypropanoic acid. The system also enabled continuous coremoval of all six PFAS in ambient conditions, with up to 96% removal and 83% defluorination over 58 d. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for how active hydrogen is generated, stored, and deployed in catalytic membranes, and identify engineered H 2 -catalytic membranes as a promising low-energy technology for destructive PFAS treatment.

title: Basin-scale evaluation of the Noah-MP land surface model for runoff and snow generation in the Missouri River Basin: insights and recommendations for parameterization scheme selection
authors: Eunsaem Cho; Eunsang Cho; Carrie M. Vuyovich; Bailing Li; Jennifer M. Jacobs
abstract: Abstract. Process-based land surface models, such as the Noah-Multiparameterization (Noah-MP) model, are widelyused for large-scale hydrologic simulations because of their flexibility in selecting multiple parameterization schemes. However, limited guidance on choosing appropriate configurations constrains their reliability in representing runoff and snowmelt dynamics across diverse land-cover and snow conditions. This study evaluates the defaultparameterization scheme and four alternative parameterization schemes in the Noah-MP land surface model, includingRunoff and Groundwater (RUN), Surface Exchange Coefficient for Heat (SFC), Frozen Soil Permeability (INF), and Snow/Soil Temperature Time Scheme (STC), across 50 Hydro-Climate Data Networks (HCDNs) in the MissouriRiver Basin. Model performance was evaluated using USGS streamflow observations and snow water equivalent (SWE) estimates from the University of Arizona dataset for 2014 to 2023. Results showed that the alternative schemes generally improved runoff simulation compared to the default scheme through better representing key hydrologicaland thermodynamic processes. Specifically, the RUN, SFC, INF, and STC experiments improved the Kling–GuptaEfficiency (KGE) by 0.19, 0.37, 0.48, and 0.14, respectively in representative subbasins, through enhancedgroundwater dynamics, reduced evapotranspiration bias, improved rapid runoff response, and more accurate SWE evolution. SWE evaluation further indicates that the STC experiment reduced the mean bias of the April–July runoff- to-maximum SWE ratio by 12–32 % in high-elevation subbasins, reflecting improved representation of snowmeltdriven runoff. These results highlight the importance of basin-specific parameterization schemes within Noah-MP toimprove hydrological prediction and water management across diverse hydroclimatic regions. The findings further indicate optimal parameterization schemes for different climates, land cover, and snow regimes.

title: Symbiotic nitrogen fixation sustains carbon sinks under warming Tibetan permafrost region
authors: Xu-Ri Xu-Ri; Jiaoneng Yu; Songbo Qu; Tian-Liang; Ribu Shama; Haojing Lei; Yuxuan Cui; Xingliang Xu; Yude Pan; Haishan Niu; Almaz Borjigidai; Eryuan Liang; Fahu Chen
abstract: Symbiotic nitrogen fixation (SNF) by legumes is a major natural source of reactive nitrogen that supports ecosystem functioning and carbon sequestration. Warming across the Tibetan Plateau alpine permafrost region may trigger substantial shifts in vegetation composition and distribution, yet the consequences for ecosystem nitrogen inputs remain poorly understood. Here, using 1047 plant samples from 323 plots across the Tibetan Plateau and 15N natural-abundance techniques, we quantify legume and non-legume nitrogen sources and regional aboveground SNF rates. Aboveground SNF is tightly linked to legume aboveground biomass, ranges from 0 to 7.43 g N m−2 yr−1, and peaks at elevations of 3600–4000 m. At the regional scale, its spatial distribution largely coincides with recent decadal gains in aboveground biomass and plant nitrogen density. Process-based simulations show that removing SNF causes severe nitrogen limitation and shifts these ecosystems from a carbon sink to a source. Our findings highlight the important role of legumes in sustaining carbon sinks in Tibetan Plateau permafrost ecosystems. Aboveground symbiotic nitrogen fixation by legumes provides a critical nitrogen source that supports plant biomass growth and sustains carbon sequestration in warming Tibetan permafrost grasslands, based on nitrogen isotope analyses and ecosystem modeling.

title: Unlocking electric vehicle flexibility in microgrids via lightweight on-charger coordination
authors: Yehui Li; Xueyuan Cui; Chongqing Kang; Thomas Morstyn; Yue Wang
abstract: The large-scale integration of electric vehicles could provide substantial flexibility for balancing renewable energy in microgrids, yet this potential remains largely constrained by uncoordinated charging. Here, we show that on-board chargers can be transformed into intelligent agents to unlock this flexibility through distributed vehicle-grid coordination. To enable such coordination under practical hardware constraints, we develop a distributed framework that embeds edge intelligence into resource-constrained chargers for autonomous charging optimization. Validated on a high-fidelity hardware-in-the-loop platform capturing microgrid cyber-physical dynamics, experimental results demonstrate that our framework reduces memory consumption by 96.1% and communication overhead by 74.3% compared to the traditional distributed coordination scheme. Moreover, unlocking this hardware-level flexibility achieves a 10.8% profit increase over the current uncoordinated situation. Importantly, the proposed framework promises profound economic, environmental, and social benefits for the future energy landscape from 2025 to 2040. Uncoordinated electric vehicle charging strains microgrids, yet advanced control exceeds charger hardware limits. Here, the authors develop a lightweight on-charger coordination framework that unlocks vehicle flexibility with low memory and communication needs.
