title: Progressive oxidative weathering raised sub-arc mantle fugacity on the Archaean Earth
authors: Hugo Moreira; Emilie Bruand; Craig D. Storey; James R. Darling; Mike Fowler; Marine Cotte; Fleurice Parat; Lorraine Tual; Bruno Dhuime
abstract: Abstract In the modern Earth, sub-arc mantle oxygen fugacity is intrinsically associated with addition of sulfur species by slab fluids. However, it is unclear to what extent recycling of volatiles controlled redox changes of the sub-arc mantle in the early Earth. Here we use sulfur K-edge micro-X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectroscopy to measure the relative abundances of S 6+ , S 4+ and S 2− in apatite inclusions hosted by geochemically characterized and dated zircons from sub-arc sanukitoid magmas that span 3.4 billion years of Earth’s geological history. The sub-arc mantle shows marked increase in oxygen fugacity between 3.4 and 3.0 billion years ago (Ga). It is substantially more oxidized than unaltered ambient upper mantle, a characteristic that cannot be explained by fractionation, degassing or intrinsic mantle processes. We propose that progressive oxidative weathering enhanced the proportion of oxidized sulfur recycled to mantle wedge sources, establishing feedback between subduction of surface materials and incrementally oxidized arc magmatism. Early subduction involving inorganic oxidation and ‘whiffs’ of oxygen between 3.4 and 2.7 Ga may have regulated an early increase in fugacity of the sub-arc mantle before the Great Oxidation Event, matching similar conditions to the modern Earth by 2.1 Ga.

title: Plasmonic metasurface microfluidic accelerates redox reactions for rapid phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing
authors: Roozbeh Siavash Moakhar; Mahsa Jalali; Tamer AbdElFatah; Sripadh Guptha Yedire; Max Petkun; Carolina del Real Mata; Ziwei He; Hamed Shieh; Geoffrey A. McKay; Rachel Corsini; Grace Reszetnik; Seyed Vahid Hamidi; Sahar Sadat Mahshid; Cédric P. Yansouni; Dao M. Nguyen
abstract: Electron-accepting chain reactions play crucial roles in diagnostics for bacterial infections, from nucleic acid amplification for bacterial identification to metabolic assays for phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing. When coupled with redox mediators, these reactions can be interrogated using an electroanalytical method. We demonstrate kinetic acceleration of loop-mediated isothermal amplification-based identification and resazurin-based phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility profiling through enhanced electromagnetic fields and modulated hot electron injection at the multilayered plasmonic metasurface-fluidic interface. We systematically investigate rounded versus sharp-apex plasmonic architectures, quantifying near-field magnitude and decay to identify geometries that maximize kinetic amplification under electrochemical readout. This approach is further combined with machine learning-assisted Gaussian fitting to improve data quantification and interpretation. Across diverse bacterial species, we achieved rapid identification with no cross-reactivity and phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing without overnight culture. In a prospective pilot clinical study of urine specimens directly from patients with suspected urinary tract infections, we observe high accuracy and strong essential and categorical agreement with standard clinical microbiology assays for bacterial identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

title: Origami-inspired folded-interlocked nanofiber aerogels for thermal insulation
authors: Xuanyu Chen; Zhao Yuan; Zhijun Zhang; Chi Hu; Shuangfei Wang; Chongxing Huang
abstract: Nanofiber aerogels (NFAs) are promising thermal insulation materials for extreme environments; however, simultaneously achieving mechanical robustness, resilience, and low thermal conductivity remains a long-standing challenge in layered NFAs, where interlaminar instability often compromises structural reliability. Here we present an origami-inspired structural engineering strategy to construct folded-interlocked nanofiber aerogels. A folded-interlocked origami skeleton, integrated with a tailored interlaminar structure, introduces geometric confinement and fiber-mediated interlaminar toughening. As a result, the aerogels exhibit high compressive strength (548.02 kPa at 80% strain) and a near-zero Poisson’s ratio. Importantly, the robust interlaminar network enhances resistance to delamination, allowing the aerogels to sustain tensile deformation up to approximately 40% strain before interlaminar failure. Meanwhile, interlaminar-guided heat-flow redistribution yields a low axial thermal conductivity of 0.035 W m−1 K−1 and pronounced anisotropic thermal insulation. This work provides an architectural strategy for designing folded-interlocked NFAs for thermal protection in aerospace and other harsh environments. Chen et al. report origami-inspired folded-interlocked nanofiber aerogels that combine mechanical resilience with low axial thermal conductivity through geometric confinement and an interlaminar fibrous network.

title: Orientation tomography of lanthanide-doped nanoprobes by polarization-resolved micro-spectroscopy
authors: Lilian Magermans; Marcello Bonetti; Thierry Gacoin; Jongwook Kim
abstract: Abstract Quantifying three-dimensional (3D) orientation is critical for understanding self-assembly and collective behavior in soft matter and biological systems. Moreover, orientational analysis of anisotropic particles can characterize locally applied forces in fluids. We present a methodology for 3D orientation tomography based on polarization-resolved spectroscopy of lanthanide-doped nanorods exhibiting multiple emission dipoles, enabling 3D orientation measurements from a single viewing angle. We develop a confocal imaging setup optimized for lanthanide luminescence and a theoretical framework to extract both the local director and order parameter in nanorod assemblies. The technique achieves 0.5 μm lateral and 1 μm axial spatial resolution and is demonstrated in dense nematic liquid-crystal assemblies, resolving complex 3D topological structures, and in microfluidic flows, mapping alignment under hydrodynamic shear. This approach provides a versatile platform for quantitative studies of collective orientation, self-assembly mechanics, and alignment induced by external forces, and can be extended to other lanthanide-labeled particles and molecular probes.

title: On predictability of slip, rupture geometry, and speed of the 2025 M7.8 Mandalay, Myanmar, earthquake
authors: Thomas Ulrich; Xiaoyu Zou; Mathilde Marchandon; Nico Schliwa; Fengzhou Tan; Alice‐Agnes Gabriel; Wenyuan Fan; Peter M. Shearer; Myo Thant; Tha Zin Htet Tin; Eric O. Lindsey; Yuri A. Fialko
abstract: Abstract The 2025 M 7.8 Mandalay earthquake ruptured ~480 km of the Sagaing Fault, producing one of the longest strike-slip events documented and impacting a vulnerable region. Here we combine remote sensing observations and numerical modeling to show that the subsurface fault geometry and slip distribution could be anticipated from pre-event observations. Along-strike variations in coseismic and interseismic deformation reveal a helix-shaped fault geometry. The average coseismic slip equals or exceeds the interseismic slip deficit, consistent with a minimally slip-predictable model. We generate an ensemble of 3D dynamic rupture models, constrained by the best-fit static slip model, then discriminate among them using independent space-geodetic, seismic, and near-field video observations. The preferred scenario begins bilaterally, then transitions to unilateral southward supershear propagation at depth, while shallow rupture remains subshear. These dynamics are shaped by localized stress heterogeneity and low fracture energy, characteristic of a structurally mature fault zone. Our approach can inform rupture scenarios in understudied regions.

title: Nanoconfinement-cooperated catalysis enables rapid tandem redox kinetics for wide-temperature lithium-sulfur batteries
authors: Tianli Li; Tao Chen; Pu Hu; Congcong Cai; Juntao Wang; Chaoqun Shang; Liwei Xiong; Yajie Li; Hanxing Liu; Jian Wang; Yaobing Wang
abstract: The slow kinetics of sulfur cathodes caused by the high energy barriers of Li + desolvation stem primarily from the structure of the inner Helmholtz plane (IHP). Herein, a synergistic strategy combining electrochemical tandem catalysis with spatial nanoconfinement is proposed to regulate the Li(solvent) x + dynamics. As a proof-of-concept, the porous covalent organic framework (denoted as TPBD) decorated MXene is in situ constructed, acting as a tandem kinetic promoter. The theoretical simulations and in situ Raman reveal that the porous TPBD layer confines the bulky Li(solvent) x + species and sieves the spatial structure with accelerated Li + diffusion kinetics. Meanwhile, MXene serves as a negatively charged substrate that helps disrupt anion-solvent interactions and reconstruct the solvation structure at the IHP, thereby enhancing Li + kinetics and sulfur redox reversibility. Encouragingly, the assembled cells demonstrate a superior Li + transference number (0.77), long-term cycling lifespan up to 1000 cycles, as well as excellent areal capacity (>6 mAh cm −2 ) at 0°C and superior rate capability at 50°C under a high sulfur loading of 7.51 mg cm −2 . The as-prepared pouch cell remains stable for over 100 cycles, validating this novel integration of catalysis and nanoconfinement for tandem kinetics in Li-S batteries.

title: Learning to infer transitively on a mental line in premotor cortex
authors: Sofia Raglio; Gabriele Di Antonio; Emiliano Brunamonti; Stefano Ferraina; Maurizio Mattia
abstract: Transitive inference (TI) is a form of deductive reasoning that enables the derivation of unknown relationships among premises. It is hypothesized that this cognitive process relies on mapping stimuli onto a "mental line," a linear workspace organized by arbitrarily assigned ranks. However, its neural basis remains unclear: Does this mental line have a neural correlate and how is it learned? This study investigates the role of dorsal premotor cortex (PMd) in encoding the hypothesized mental line as monkeys acquire item relationships for motor decisions. Findings reveal that PMd multiunit activity organizes along a theoretically predicted direction, supporting a geometrical model that explains behavior. Moreover, a learning process is observed, where the mental line rotates to align with motor planning.

title: Geochemical clustering reveals cryptic eruptions and tephra correlations from Antarctic fumarolic ice-cave archives
authors: Paola Del Carlo; Paola Del Carlo; Alessandro Musu; Alessio Di Roberto; Giuseppe Re; Gaetano Giudice; Mónica Ágreda López; Maurizio Petrelli
abstract: Abstract Volcanic deposits preserved within Antarctic fumarolic ice caves provide rare access to sub-ice eruptive records hidden beneath the ice cap. Here we present the first integrated textural, petrological, and geochemical characterisation of 21 tephra samples from three summit ice caves at Mount Melbourne (Northern Victoria Land, Antarctica). Major and trace-element glass compositions, combined with published datasets, were analysed using multivariate statistical workflows. Dimensionality reduction and clustering identified a distinct compositional group with no known equivalent in the existing Mount Melbourne record, suggesting that at least one previously unrecognised Holocene eruption occurred within the investigated Fumarolic Ice Caves. Correspondence between Fumarolic Ice Cave deposits and volcanic signatures in marine sediment, englacial sequences, and other proximal-distal records refined Mount Melbourne’s eruptive history and strengthened tephra correlations across archives. More broadly, sub-ice tephra archives can reveal hidden eruptive histories relevant to volcanic hazard assessment in polar regions.

title: From scrap to prime: Designing high-performance alloys from dirty feedstocks with machine learning
authors: Chao Yang; Bo Peng; Binhan Sun; Qingzhou Tao; Yuxin Zeng; Lijun Zhang; Da Shu; Jian Lü; Dierk Raabe; Liuliu Han; Wei Ye
abstract: Producing alloys from recycled metals via secondary synthesis can markedly cut energy use, greenhouse-gas emissions, and dependence on scarce, strategically important elements relative to primary routes. The central obstacle is the feedstock itself: Scrap is chemically heterogeneous and unpredictable, a "dirty" mix whose impurities typically embrittle materials. Conventional strategies address this challenge by diluting impurities through the addition of virgin material, thereby restricting scrap utilization, limiting microstructural design freedom, and undermining cost and sustainability benefits. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different, data-driven paradigm that deliberately reverses a five-millennia-old metallurgical injunction: Rather than purifying the alloy, we design the alloy to accommodate and exploit its contaminants. Using a model ductile iron representative of 120 million metric tons of heavily contaminated scrap, we couple experiments with deep-neural-network optimization to identify chemically robust, impurity-tolerant processing windows. The resulting "dirty" irons retain ductility and strength by integrating impurity effects into a purposeful microstructure, rather removing them. The approach achieves complete recyclability, an 8.1% reduction in manufacturing cost, and mechanical gains of up to 15.2% in ultimate tensile strength and 73.2% in elongation at fracture. Crucially, it overcomes the canonical strength-ductility trade-off while enabling far greater scrap utilization and material circularity. By endowing alloys with a practical "gene of scrap compatibility," this strategy reframes alloy design for a resource-constrained future and advances a mass-conserving circular economy for metals.

title: From ancient practice to modern innovation solving the clay mineral puzzle in brickmaking
authors: Sen Wang; Lloyd Gainey; Lihui Liu; Zijun Zeng; Shusheng Xiao; Runliang Zhu; Sara Jane Couperthwaite; Yuantong Gu; Yunfei Xi
abstract: Abstract Clay minerals are the most crucial constituents in brickmaking clays, yet the specific role of different clay minerals remain poorly understood due to their natural coexistence and formidable challenges of separation. Here, we design a kaolinite-illite-quartz-feldspar system through a multiple-stage purification strategy, enabling direct evaluation of two of the most critical clay minerals for brick making - kaolinite and illite. Precise tuning the initial clay mineral assemblage yields brick strengths up to 8.5 times the ASTM C62 Grade MW requirement, without upgrading existing production methods. Mineralogical mechanisms responsible for substantial strength enhancement are revealed. Extensive analyses of 60 brick formulations uncovered a breakdown of conventional linear relationships among different brick properties due to the temperature-dependent responses of kaolinite and illite; specific formation pathways of mullite and amorphous phases; and over-firing defects above 1200 °C due to K + -induced fluxing from illite. Notably, a previously unrecognized negative correlation between mullite and brick strength is identified, suggesting a need to reconsider the widely held assumption of mullite as a strengthening phase. This work not only presents insights for optimizing high-strength brick formulations but also opens avenues for investigating the intricate contributions of distinct starting components to key brick performance.

title: Citizens’ assemblies propose ambitious climate policy but impacts remain limited
authors: J.T. Pfeffer; Hannah Einhauser; Johanna Hauke; Kira Hoffmann; Lisa Ruf; Milena Weber; Florian Weckbecker; Marlene Wellhausen; Jens Newig
abstract: Abstract Climate citizens’ assemblies convene randomly selected citizens who, after structured learning and deliberation, develop policy recommendations. Yet, whether they produce more ambitious recommendations and influence political decisions remains contested. Here we conduct a comparative, counterfactual assessment of 488 recommendations from five national and one state-level assembly in Western Europe, drawing on document analysis and expert interviews. The results show that citizens consistently proposed more ambitious climate measures than existing government policy. Recommendations sometimes influenced policy by adding momentum, enriching plans, breaking deadlocks or introducing novel ideas, but such influence was rare. Only the French assembly shows substantial policy impact, with one-third of its recommendations having influenced policy, due to strong power delegation, political leadership and resulting public pressure. In the other cases, policy impact was minimal or absent. These findings show that citizens’ assemblies can raise policy ambition, but translating recommendations into political decisions depends strongly on political conditions.

title: Weathering-derived calcium supports carbon storage in grassland soils
authors: E. W. Slessarev; H. R. Goertzen; Rebecca A. Lybrand; Karis J. McFarlane; Jennifer Pett‐Ridge; Noah W. Sokol; D. G. Zaharescu; K. Georgiou
abstract: Abstract Dark colored grassland soils, known as Mollisols, are intensively farmed and rich in organic matter, and hence have an important role in the carbon cycle. Organic carbon storage in Mollisols may result from interactions between organic matter and calcium released by carbonate and silicate weathering. Here we test this hypothesis by using a geochemical model to simulate calcium release from weathering in soils across the USA. We find that calcium released by mineral weathering is associated with soil organic carbon storage and that this effect is stronger in Mollisols than in non-Mollisols. Our model also shows that agriculture has increased calcium inputs to cultivated USA Mollisols 4-5 fold, indicating that humans have fundamentally changed the geochemical conditions that sustain organic carbon in these soils. By implication, moderating the quantity of and timing of calcium release may help to preserve and restore carbon in the world’s most intensively farmed landscapes.

title: U.S. oil and gas methane emission intensity declined 2019–2024 with little indication of federal policy impact
authors: Ao Chen; William Daniels; Ziting Huang; Arvind Pawan Ravikumar; Sarah Marie Jordaan; Zhen Zhang; Leyang Feng; Hanyu Liu; Lee Thomas Murray; Xueying Yu; Dylan C. Gaeta; Kristan L. Morgan; Jialuo Yuan; Scot M. Miller
abstract: Abstract The U.S. federal government undertook a flurry of new actions to monitor and regulate methane emissions beginning in years 2021 and 2022, including the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA). The IRA and Waste Emissions Charge (WEC) represent a historic legislative effort to regulate U.S. methane emissions, yet its early effectiveness remains empirically unverified. Here we estimate changes in U.S. oil and gas methane emissions during 2019--2024 using an inverse model constrained by satellite observations. We find no detectable inflection point in U.S. oil and gas methane emissions in the years following these legislative and regulatory actions. Although methane emissions intensity from the oil and gas sector declined by 9.3--13.6\% during 2019--2024, this trend likely reflects gradual technological, operational, and regulatory developments rather than any abrupt shift associated with federal policy. Furthermore, we identify a divergence in inventory reliability: state-level inventories align with satellite estimates in the highest emitting states with greenhouse gas (GHG) emission targets but underestimate emissions by a factor of about 4 in the highest emitting states without GHG targets. Our results underscore the limitations of transient legislative signals, suggesting that without long-term regulatory durability, the industry lacks the incentive to commit to methane emission reductions.

title: Technical note: A physically based correction of WRF temperature using atmospheric lapse rates for high-resolution hydrological simulations in a glacierized catchment
authors: Florentin Hofmeister; Xinyang Fan; Madlene Pfeiffer; Ben Marzeion; Bettina Schaefli; Gabriele Chiogna
abstract: Abstract. High-elevation alpine catchments are particularly affected by the global rise in temperature. Understanding the drivers of climate-induced changes in the hydrological response of these catchments in the past is relevant for developing future adaptation strategies for water resources and risk management. However, the study of long-term changes since the last Little Ice Age (around 1850) is strongly limited by the availability of hydrometeorological observation data. Regional climate models (RCMs) can bridge this limitation and provide comprehensive meteorological forcing data for hydrological models (HM). We used the Weather Research & Forecasting Model (WRF) to dynamically downscale a global reanalysis product (20CRv3) to a 2 km x 2 km spatial and 1 h temporal resolution from 1850 to 2015 as forcing for an HM (WaSiM). The main challenge is transferring the forcing data to the much finer grid resolution (i.e., 25 m) of the HM, considering the complex topography and plausible sub-daily precipitation and temperature lapse rates (TLRs). Thus, we developed a workflow for extracting and transferring hourly TLRs from the WRF atmosphere to the small-scale topography of the HM domain. In addition, we corrected WRF precipitation frequencies with observation data and re-distributed the precipitation according to the small-scale topography. Our study demonstrates the impact of TLRs computed from different WRF layers (i.e., 2 m and free atmosphere) on the HM results of a highly glaciated Alpine catchment in the European Alps. In a multi-data evaluation procedure, we found that the TLRs and the HM results are significantly dependent on the coarse surface properties of WRF. Temperature-sensitive processes such as snow and glacier evolution, as well as the streamflow response, are more realistically simulated when the HM is forced by TLRs originating from the WRF free atmosphere rather than with simulated near-surface temperature. The HM results are also consistent with observation data over a simulation period beginning in 1969, suggesting the corrected WRF temperature can reliably reproduce the non-stationarity in local temperature observations. Our study addresses several aspects, limitations, and potential solutions in applying a standard modeling chain of an RCM and a physics-based HM for climate sensitivity studies in high-elevation alpine regions.

title: Soil proteogenomics uncover microbial strategies for soil depth-specific carbon cycling under whole-soil warming conditions
authors: Ulaş Karaöz; Ricardo Eloy Alves; Nikola Tolić; Rosalie Chu; Carrie Nicora; Jason G. Toyoda; Emiley A. Eloe‐Fadrosh; Margaret S. Torn; Eoin Brodie
abstract: Soils are Earth's largest carbon reservoir, yet microbial mechanisms controlling decomposition, and their warming response, remain poorly resolved, especially in subsoils. Using genome-resolved proteogenomics within a replicated whole-soil warming experiment (0-90 cm, +4 °C, 7.5 years) we map microbial traits, their depth stratification, and warming responses. Depth is the dominant driver of microbial community and trait structure. Depth-wise, metabolism converge on low-molecular-weight and C1 compounds, challenging glucose-centric models, with surface soils enriched in methanol oxidation and deep soils in alcohol fermentation, CO oxidation and N₂ fixation. Abundant sialidases in deep soils implicate glycoproteins as a key carbon source. Warming effects are smaller and decrease over time but are depth-specific: surface soils show enhanced amino sugar and sugar alcohol transport, phosphorus mobilization, and stress tolerance, whereas mid- and deep soils exhibit stimulated C1 metabolism, CO oxidation, and altered nitrogen turnover. These depth-specific microbial trait shifts may critically influence soil carbon-climate feedbacks.

title: Securing critical rare-earth supply through end-of-life NdFeB magnets recycling via molten salt electrolysis with consumable Mg-cathode
authors: Jiayang Wei; Weiyuqing He; Qiance Liu; Xin Chun Lu; Peng Wang; Wei‐Li Song; Osamu Takeda; Gang Liu; Kazuyo Matsubae; Yongxiang Yang; Hongmin Zhu; Shuqiang Jiao
abstract: Recycling end-of-life (EoL) NdFeB magnets is critical for securing supply of rare-earth element neodymium in the low-carbon transition. We develop a molten salt electrolysis recycling approach using EoL NdFeB magnet anodes and a consumable solid magnesium cathode, operating at 548–650 °C and 0.75–3 A·cm−2 cathodic current density. Selective neodymium dissolution and in situ formation of a liquid Mg– (12.0–15.1 mol%) Nd alloy with average current efficiency of 98.4% are achieved. With high recycling efficiency and continuous operation, this approach overcomes neodymium collection and scalability barriers of conventional chloride electrolysis. Life-cycle assessment shows that the proposed process lowers climate change impacts to 17.36–18.18 kg CO2 eq. kg⁻¹ Nd, approximately 15% of that of primary production. Techno-economic analysis shows that neodymium metal production costs fall to 90.0 USD kg⁻¹ Nd at the 3000 A scale scenario, which is approximately one-third lower than the sales price of Nd metal. Such approach demonstrates significant potential for industrial-scale application and facilitates the integration of neodymium recycling into circular economy strategies. Molten-salt electrolysis with a consumable magnesium cathode recovers neodymium from end-of-life NdFeB magnets at high current efficiency, while life-cycle and economic analyses indicate potential for industrial-scale recycling.

title: Impact-based flood-damage assessment in Japan under longitudinal typhoon-track perturbations and levee-height variations during Hagibis (2019)
authors: Xiaoyang Li; Kei Yoshimura; Hironori Fudeyasu
abstract: Abstract Impact-based flood-damage assessment integrates hydrometeorological information with vulnerability and exposure data to generate comprehensive evaluation of flood damage. This study uses the Integrated Land Simulator to assemble an impact-based flood-damage assessment framework for Typhoon Hagibis (2019), one of the most powerful typhoons to strike Japan in recent years. To systematically evaluate how typhoon-track position and levee height influence flood damage, we conduct longitudinal typhoon-track perturbation experiments and levee-height variation scenario analyses. Here we show that the flood damage is highly sensitive to small typhoon-track shifts, with a 0.2° longitudinal shift causing an average damage difference of 83.3 billion JPY. A 1.0° eastward shift causes the highest damage in Kanto and across Japan, mainly around Tokyo, while 1.6° and 0.4° westward shifts produce the greatest damage in Kinki and Chubu, mainly around Osaka and Nagoya, respectively. The levee-height sensitivity experiments show an average flood-damage reduction of approximately 9.1 billion JPY for each 10% increase in levee height.

title: Epitaxial-strain engineering of supported tensile noble metallene oxides for enhanced oxidation catalysis
authors: Shoujie Zhang; Dong Lin; Anwen Yu; Haifeng Qi; Zhongyu Jiang; Xiuhui Zheng; Xiang Feng; Yongning Yang; Zhikang Fu; Sheng Dai; Lina Li; Aiyong Wang; Yun Guo; Wangcheng Zhan; Li Wang
abstract: Abstract Supported two-dimensional noble metal oxides (metallene oxides) hold great promise for heterogeneous catalysis owing to their maximized surface exposure and tunable electronic structures. However, their high surface energy and low oxidation potentials make them intrinsically unstable under reaction conditions. Here, we report an epitaxial strain strategy to stabilize and modulate the electronic structure of supported PtO 2 metallene oxide. By employing rutile TiO 2 and rutile SnO 2 supports with distinct lattice parameters, we achieve epitaxial growth of PtO 2 metallene oxide layers with controlled strain states, where the larger-lattice SnO 2 substrate imposes biaxial tensile strain on PtO 2 . The tensile-strained PtO 2 /SnO 2 exhibits a reconfigured Pt–O electronic environment that simultaneously improves structural resilience and enhances the intrinsic reactivity of PtO 2 , delivering markedly improved methane oxidation performance with a T 90 of 370 °C (versus 434 °C for PtO 2 /TiO 2 and 469 °C for PtO x /Al 2 O 3 ) and <1% conversion loss over 38 h under both dry and wet conditions. Moreover, this epitaxial strain strategy is generalizable to other environmentally relevant oxidation reactions and rutile-type noble metal oxides, establishing tensile strain imposed by epitaxial lattice matching as a general principle for stabilizing atomically thin noble metal oxides while tuning their electronic structure.

title: Enhancing fairness in climate action through policy packages
authors: Toon Vandyck; Umed Temursho; Florian Landis; David Klenert; Matthias Weitzel
abstract: Abstract Achieving a fair transition to climate neutrality requires a careful balancing of policy options. Here we quantitatively evaluate the equity implications of different European Union climate policy packages, considering pricing, regulation via standards, subsidies and transfers. Leveraging an integrated modelling framework, we show that standards limit impact variability within income groups, whereas carbon pricing with transfer-based revenue recycling offsets regressive impacts between income groups. Restricting climate policy implementation to either option, therefore, gives rise to a trade-off between horizontal and vertical equity. We then demonstrate numerically how a multi-instrument budget-neutral policy package can resolve this trade-off. Adopting a broader equity perspective that encompasses both horizontal and vertical equity shifts the preferred policy mix towards a combination of standards, pricing, subsidies and transfers. These results provide an explicit, quantified, equity-based rationale for the adoption and acceptability of comprehensive climate policy packages, offering a more nuanced view on policy design.

title: Disrupting the NAD+/NAM metabolic ratio driven by IL-1β inflammatory response potentiates chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy in mice
authors: Fuxue Xing; Hongwei Lv; Liang Wang; Yun Feng; Wei Xiang; Lu Wu; Guoqing Jiang; Yue Ma; 孙晓艳; Zixin Wu; Kunqing Xiao; Qiuyu Lu; Min Zhang; Qianni Zong; Guishuai Lv
abstract: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) replenishment sensitizes tumors to immunotherapy. However, chemotherapy-induced NAD+ metabolic reprogramming remains poorly understood. Here, we show that chemotherapy induces a macrophage-dependent IL-1β inflammatory response and NAD+ metabolic reprogramming, thereby conferring chemoresistance via CD44. Mechanistically, IL-1β-induced NAD+ salvage cooperates with the clearance of nicotinamide (NAM), the physiological inhibitor of the NAD+-consuming enzymes sirtuins, to drive CD44-mediated chemoresistance by boosting the NAD+/NAM ratio for sirtuin activation. NAM phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT)-mediated NAD+ salvage recycles NAD+ from NAM and further triggers serine biosynthesis, ultimately supporting NAM N-methyltransferase (NNMT)-mediated NAM clearance. Importantly, NAMPT inhibition disrupts the NAD+/NAM ratio and mitigates CD44-mediated chemoresistance and NK cell dysfunction, ultimately enhancing the efficacy of chemoimmunotherapy when combined with IL-2 across multiple preclinical models of solid tumors. Thus, our findings underscore the NAD+/NAM ratio as a metabolic therapeutic target for enhancing chemotherapy and NK cell-based chemoimmunotherapy efficacy. NAD+ metabolic pathways regulate tumor growth and sensitivity to therapeutic treatment. However, the effects of chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy regimens on NAD metabolism remain unclear. Here, the authors identify a macrophage-driven IL-1β inflammatory signaling that regulates the NAD + /NAM metabolic ratio to drive CD44-mediated chemoresistance and NK cell dysfunction and show that disruption of the NAD + /NAM ratio sensitises tumors to chemoimmunotherapy across multiple preclinical mouse models.

title: Current aviation roadmaps are not within planetary boundaries
authors: Bastien Païs; Alexandre Gondran; Lorie Hamelin; Florian Simatos
abstract: Abstract Aviation decarbonization roadmaps predominantly rely on replacing fossil kerosene with alternative jet fuels, yet the systemic impact of these alternatives on planetary boundaries other than climate change has not been quantified. Here we integrate prospective life-cycle inventories with the planetary boundaries framework to evaluate the absolute impacts of aviation roadmaps as time-dependent trajectories, rather than endpoint snapshots. Across scenarios to 2050, we find that fuel-switch-centered roadmaps do not achieve sustainability, persistently transgress the climate change and biosphere integrity core boundaries, and exert large demands for energy, land, freshwater and CO 2 capture that challenge their feasibility. Slower traffic growth brings aviation closer to its share of the safe operating space in terms of lowering energy demand, but respecting additional planetary boundaries requires air traffic to decline by at least 7.2% yr −1 . Our results show that aligning aviation with Earth’s safe operating space cannot be achieved through fuel substitution alone and requires governance strategies that combine supply-side solutions with explicit demand-side measures.

title: Controlled crosslink cleavage and phase separation enable highly stretchable and strong 3D-printed hydrogel for soft robotics
authors: Liangshen Zhao; Jianrong Cai; Qilin Qian; Shengming Zhang; Chenhao Wang; Ting Chen; Chaonan Xiao; Chunling Ren; Qingmei Zeng; Bingkun Bao; Qiuning Lin; Hongen Liao; Linyong Zhu; Boyu Zhang
abstract: Soft robots operate safely in delicate, confined environments and require materials that combine softness and large deformation in complex architectures. Digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing enables such structures, but rapid curing fixes networks with short strands, limiting extensibility of printed hydrogels. Here we report a controlled post-print decrosslinking strategy that decouples shape fixation from network maturation to yield highly stretchable, strong DLP-printed hydrogels. In this design, photo-triggered, base-cleavable coupling between o-nitrobenzyl acetal and (meth)acrylate groups establishes a dense network for printing and shape fixation. Subsequent alkaline cleavage restores chain mobility and lengthens network strands, while hydrophobic side-group modification induces phase-separated domains that enhance strength. The resulting hydrogels reach 1100% strain at break and 3.7 MPa tensile strength, combining high stretchability with high strength. This performance enables pneumatic actuators with 8-fold volumetric expansion and payload transport in confined fluidic environments. Our strategy provides a soft material platform for 3D-printed soft robotic systems requiring large, reversible deformation. Soft robots require soft and highly deformable materials in complex architectures. Digital light processing 3D printing enables such structures, but rapid curing creates short-strand networks that limit hydrogel extensibility. Here the authors report a post-print decrosslinking strategy that decouples shape fixation from network maturation producing highly stretchable, strong DLP-printed hydrogels.

title: A multi-stage engineering framework for feasible scheduling of large-scale energy batch transport systems
authors: Renfu Tu; Qi Liao; Hao Zhang; Zhengbing Li; Rui Qiu; Guangtao Fu; Enrico Zio; Yongtu Liang
abstract: The energy transition is driving batch transport systems toward multi-product, high-frequency operations, with more batches and smaller batch volumes. However, strong couplings among material flows, operational decisions and temporal constraints make large-scale scheduling increasingly difficult, often rendering direct optimization computationally infeasible within practical engineering timeframes. This challenge is particularly pronounced in large-scale multi-product pipeline systems. To address this, this study proposes a multi-stage engineering framework that enables feasible and scalable scheduling of large-scale, batch-centric transport systems. The framework integrates two complementary mechanisms: a coarse-to-fine feasibility identification strategy that progressively narrows the admissible operational space, and a divide-and-conquer temporal decomposition strategy that partitions long scheduling horizons into tractable sub-horizons. The proposed framework is validated using two distinct industrial-scale pipeline systems. In a six-product benchmark, the framework achieves zero or negligible optimality gaps. For a complex branching network, it obtains feasible, high-quality schedules within the engineering time limit, whereas direct optimization fails to achieve a gap below 3%. Temporal decomposition reduces active binary variables and improves solution quality by over 50%. The framework provides a generalizable approach for large-scale batch transport and emerging multi-carrier energy infrastructures. A multi-stage framework enables feasible, high-quality scheduling of large-scale energy transport systems that challenge conventional optimization, supporting more efficient operation of emerging multi-carrier energy infrastructure.

title: Neuronal signatures of successful one-shot memory in mid-level visual cortex
authors: Grace F DiRisio; Cheng Xue; Marlene R. Cohen
abstract: High-capacity, one-shot visual recognition memory challenges theories of learning and neural coding because it requires rapid, robust, and durable representations. Most studies have focused on the hippocampus and other higher areas. However, behavioral evidence demonstrating links between image properties and memorability and revealing image specificity of visual memory suggests an important role for mid-level visual cortex. We tested the hypothesis that area V4 contains signals critical for recognition memory in two male rhesus macaques. Our task increased difficulty, allowing comparisons of neuronal population responses on correct and error trials. We observed signatures of several proposed memory mechanisms including magnitude coding, repetition suppression, sparse coding, and population response consistency, but only sparse coding and population response consistency predicted behavior. Familiar images also evoked faster dynamics, consistent with pattern completion. These findings demonstrate that fast, high-capacity memory is supported by neural codes in mid-level sensory cortex independent of stimulus features per se, highlighting its role in distributed memory networks. Neural mechanisms underlying one-shot memory are not fully understood. In this study, macaque monkeys were trained to perform a continuous image recognition task and simultaneously recorded from groups of neurons in area V4. The authors found that the perceptual building blocks of fast, high-capacity memory are present in mid-level sensory cortex.

title: Global rise of a wheat pathogen through two-stage evolutionary emergence coupled with aerial dispersal
authors: Siyue Zhang; Yuxiang Li; Gangming Zhan; Jingchen Zhao; Zhibo Zhang; Hanzheng Liu; Umer Basu; K. Kanyuka; Huw Davis; Zhuoma Qucuo; Fei Tao; Haifeng Gao; Guangkuo Li; Jinbiao Ma; Qiang Yao
abstract: The rise of plant pathogens following crop domestication and their subsequent global spread pose persistent threats to food security, yet the mechanisms underlying host jumps and rapid adaptation in obligate biotrophs remain unclear. Using 319 Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici (Pst) genomes and virulence phenotypes of 234 isolates across six continents, we construct its origin and global dissemination. Our analyses support a two-stage emergence model: P. striiformis sensu stricto originated and diversified in the Himalayan region, subsequently a P. striiformis s. str. lineage jumped to domesticated wheat in the Fertile Crescent, giving rise to epidemic lineage (Pst) and spreading worldwide with wheat cultivation. This host jump triggered demographic expansion and selective sweeps, while GWAS identified region-specific virulence loci shaped by resistant cultivars. Overlay of air trajectory and dispersal simulations identified atmospheric corridors consistent with genomic migration patterns, supporting a historical role for long-distance aerial transport in the pathogen’s global spread. Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici, an obligate fungal pathogen, threatens wheat production worldwide. Using 319 genomes and virulence data from 234 isolates globally, this study constructs its two-stage emergence and global dissemination, supporting a historical role for long-distance aerial transport.

title: A water-pinning hot spot drives templated tau aggregation
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
authors: Chung-Ta Han; Karen Tsay; Samuel Lobo; Saeed Najafi; Kieran Monahan; Erica Hong; M. Scott Shell; Joan‐Emma Shea; Songi Han
abstract: Tau assembles into fibrillar aggregates that are pathological hallmarks of a group of neurodegenerative diseases collectively called tauopathies. Templated aggregation of naïve tau to seeding-competent fibrils that proceed from cell to cell is a key driver of prion-like progression of tauopathies. This study tests the hypothesis that tau, an intrinsically disordered protein, achieves in-register stacking to form seed-competent fibrils by a pinning action of tau to each other and/or the seed surface via a single dominant hotspot to avoid mismatch in tau stacking to fibrils. Structured solvation water has been proposed to be a signature of such hot spots at both the tau fibril-end surface and soluble tau monomers. Although jR2R3-P301L tau exhibits a heterogeneous hydration landscape in its intrinsically disordered state, with enhanced water structuring near the P301L mutation site, it is unclear whether a localized hotspot exists at the fibril end surface and surface water facilitates the initial contacts in templated aggregation. Using rapid 1 H- 15 N SOFAST-HMQC NMR to track seed-induced aggregation of jR2R3-P301L in real time, complemented by molecular dynamics simulation of fibril surface hydration, we identify a residue-specific pinning hotspot that is prone to dewetting followed by sequential folding and incorporation of the remaining segment in a two-step dock-and-lock process. Site-specific spin labeling further demonstrates that blocking this pinning hotspot disrupts templated aggregation, leading to shorter fibrils. The identification of a dominant pinning site will facilitate the rational design of binders to effectively disrupt fibril extension or serve as diagnostic or therapeutic strategies.

title: Impact of climate change on the photovoltaic power potential in Sweden across 21st century
authors: Tianqi Ruan; Fuxing Wang; Björn Laumert; Aitor Aldama Campino; Wujun Wang
abstract: Abstract Solar photovoltaic generation strongly relies on weather conditions, which will be affected by future climate change. Traditional methods for estimating photovoltaic generation potential often overlook detailed installation factors and snow impacts, leading to inaccuracies in high-latitude areas. We assess future photovoltaic system performance in Sweden using a validated photovoltaic installation model that incorporates air temperature, radiation and snow conditions. Applying this model to four Swedish cities under low- and high-emission climate change scenarios and three climate simulations, we project an approximate 5% increase in photovoltaic generation relative to the historical period with optimal installation angle. The combined effects of air temperature and snowfall are as crucial as solar radiation for photovoltaic generation in Sweden, so the photovoltaic generation change will be relatively limited by 2100. Optimized tilt angles are obtained for all the four cities, which could increase photovoltaic generation by 3-6% compared to the commercial angle. The findings also provide valuable insights into photovoltaic potential in a changing climate.

title: HCV incidence and prevalence trends among people who use drugs in France 2004 to 2023
authors: Chiara Elisa Sabbatini; Yann Le Strat; Christophe Bonaldi; Cécile Brouard; Martin Audran; Leïla Saboni; Jean‐Baptiste Richard; Amélie David; Catherine Gaudy‐Graffin; Stéphane Chevaliez; Francis Barin; Karl Stéfic; Marie Jauffret‐Roustide
abstract: Abstract Hepatitis C virus (HCV) remains a key public health challenge, particularly among people who use and inject drugs (PWUD, PWID). While direct-acting antivirals (DAA) have revolutionized HCV treatment, meeting the WHO’s 2030 elimination target requires accurate estimation of incidence and prevalence to guide prevention and care. We analyze cross-sectional surveys conducted in France in 2004, 2013, and 2023, recruiting PWUD at harm reduction services and collecting behavioral and biological data. We estimate age-and time-dependent prevalence of HCV antibodies and HCV RNA using multivariate regression models while incidence was estimated from two-state transmission models. The demographic profile of PWUD has aged over time (mean age 35 years in 2004 vs. 44 in 2023) while injection prevalence remained stable (61.7% in 2023). Between 2013 and 2023, HCV burden declined substantially: HCV RNA prevalence fell from 19.4% (95% CI 16.3–23.0) to 9.5% (7.2–12.3) among all PWUD, and from 29.6% to 14.5% among PWID. Incidence among PWID decreased from 6.5 (4.1–8.0) to 2.4 (1.4–4.2) per 100 person-years. These reductions likely reflect the combined impact of DAA scale-up and harm reduction policies, marking substantial progress toward elimination targets. However, ongoing transmission highlights persistent barriers requiring targeted public health actions.

title: A method quantifying soil melanin to understand fungal impacts on soil carbon stability
authors: Sylwia Adamczyk; Bartosz Adamczyk
abstract: Abstract Fungal necromass, particularly dead microbial cells rich in melanin, is an important contributor to long-term soil carbon stabilization. Progress in understanding the role of soil melanin is limited by the lack of validated analytical methods. DNA-based approaches estimate only the genetic potential for melanin production and therefore provide indirect evidence of melanin occurrence. To directly assess soil melanin, we evaluated spectroscopic and spectrophotometric assays; however, both approaches proved insufficiently specific due to interference from chemically related compounds. Here, we introduce a liquid chromatography method that enables quantification of major fungal melanin types in soils. By enabling direct quantification of fungal melanin in soil, this framework allows longstanding hypotheses regarding melanized fungal necromass and soil carbon stabilization to be tested mechanistically. Here, we show with the proposed method that soil melanin concentrations are strongly correlated with total soil carbon, supporting a central role for fungal melanin in long-term soil carbon stabilization.

title: Onset of zircon decomposition during saprolitic weathering
authors: Martin Li; Mei-Fu Zhou
abstract: Abstract Zircon is conventionally considered as refractory in supergene environments, enabling the preservation of geochemical records for tracing various Earth’s processes and the use of the zircon structure as a nuclear waste form. However, how refractory zircon is during weathering, especially when crystalline and in an early stage of weathering, is unknown. In this study, we demonstrate that crystalline zircon would start to weather during an early-stage saprolitic weathering. Nano-scale examination reveals that weathering of zircon proceeds through dissolution of primary, crystalline zircon and precipitation of secondary, amorphous zircon. Non-formula elements, like U, Th and heavy rare earth elements, are uptake and structurally incorporated in this process. Thereby, metamictisation of the zircon would accelerate and eventually promote the dissolution of zircon. In supergene environments, zircon would steadily weather, calling for further evaluation on the geological and environmental applications of zircon.

title: Long-term nitrous acid evolution modulates ozone and secondary aerosol variations in global megacities
authors: Xuan Li; Can Ye; Huabin Dong; Xuezhen Xu; Haichao Wang; Xiaorui Chen; Zhaofeng Tan; Xuefei Ma; Shiyi Chen; Keding Lu; Yuanhang Zhang
abstract: Nitrous acid (HONO) is a crucial urban source of HOx radicals, promoting surface ozone (O3) and secondary fine particle (PM2.5) formation, yet its long-term evolution and air-quality impacts remain poorly constrained. Here, using a deep neural network established on worldwide field campaigns, we reconstruct global surface HONO distributions. Typical megacities exhibited contrasting trends in 2005–2021, marked by a sharp decline in Beijing (−47.4% in 2013–2021), an increase in Delhi (+10.0% in 2005–2018), and slight decreases in London, New York and Los Angeles. These HONO changes are identified as major driver of O3 and particulate nitrate variations, outweighing contributions of conventional NOx and volatile organic compounds abatement in Beijing and Delhi, while showing comparable impacts in the remaining cities. A fused data-driven framework further uncovers regime-dependent HONO reduction strategies, prioritizing NOx control in summer and co-reduction of NOx, PM2.5 and direct combustion emissions in winter, to accelerate O3 and PM2.5 joint mitigation. Deep learning reveals a sharp decline of HONO in China, modest drops in EU and US but an increase in India. HONO changes drive O3 and PM2.5 variations, outweighing traditional NOx and VOC control, calling for HONO-targeted air quality management.

title: Intrinsically flexible inorganic piezoelectric subnanowire enables wireless wearable bioelectronics for non-invasive multimodal human-machine interfacing
authors: Xin Xu; Xiaoya Wang; Yize Cui; Qingda Liu; Xun Wang
abstract: Piezoelectric electronic skin (PE-skin) offers a significant advantage in detecting minute forces, making it highly promising for human-computer interaction in health management and medical rehabilitation. However, PE-skin often faces challenges in real-time, wireless transmission of sensing data, which can compromise both data accuracy and user comfort. Here, we report the synthesis of an inorganic piezoelectric polyoxometalate-based subnanowire, ZnBiPMo12, which possesses intrinsic flexibility and chirality, a piezoelectric coefficient of 24.9 pC/N, and notable ferroelectricity. Leveraging its piezoelectric response, ZnBiPMo12-based PE-skin (1) demonstrates high elasticity and sensitivity to tiny pressures in the range of 0.045-0.319 N. Building on this, a wireless, wearable bioelectronic (WBE) device (1A) is fabricated through multi-level assembly, enabling non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals, including subtle muscle contractions, blinking, breathing, and all-day heart rate. By integrating a machine learning system, a 1-based facial-computer interface (1B) can accurately recognize nine emotional expressions and twelve spoken words. This work not only introduces a typical inorganic piezoelectric material with intrinsic flexibility but also demonstrates scalable manufacturing from subnanomaterials to wireless WBEs, paving the way for non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals and advanced human-computer interaction. Piezoelectric materials enable bioelectronic sensing by converting mechanical stimuli into electrical signals. Xu et al. introduce intrinsically flexible polyoxometalate-based subnanowires and demonstrate their scalable integration into wireless wearable systems for human physiological monitoring.

title: Hydrogeological controls on radial collector well intake: interactions among aquifer properties, clogging, and lateral hydraulics
authors: S.-C. Lee; Min‐Ho Koo; Jaeyun Jung
abstract: Radial collector well (RCW) intake is governed by complex interactions among aquifer properties, river–aquifer connectivity, clogging processes, and hydraulic losses within collector laterals. This study investigates these controls using a coupled aquifer–lateral flow formulation implemented in MODFLOW, in which laterals are represented as Drain cells with iteratively updated heads and conductance to account for near-lateral resistance and internal frictional and momentum losses. A conceptual model was used to examine aquifer hydraulic conductivity and anisotropy, aquitard properties, river-to-caisson distance, filter-pack and riverbed clogging, caisson operational head, and lateral design parameters. Intake increased with aquifer hydraulic conductivity, although the response became nonlinear as lateral head losses intensified. Vertical hydraulic resistance caused by anisotropy or aquitards reduced intake and, under some conditions, produced a finite optimal river-to-caisson distance. Well clogging exerted a much stronger influence than riverbed clogging, and severe reductions in filter-pack hydraulic conductivity reduced intake to near-zero levels. Among the lateral design variables, lateral diameter had the strongest effect, particularly in high-conductivity aquifers. Longer laterals were more effective in low-conductivity aquifers, whereas adding laterals was more beneficial in high-conductivity aquifers, where groundwater could be supplied from multiple directions. These results show that RCW performance depends on the location and magnitude of the dominant hydraulic resistance within the coupled river–aquifer–well system. The findings provide a process-based framework for RCW design, performance interpretation, and clogging management under site-specific hydrogeological conditions.

title: Extensive genomic diversity in Desulfovibrio reveals species-specific functional traits associated with disease
authors: Tingting Zheng; Isabel Keidel; Hélène Omer; Akshat Joshipura; Aurélie Cenier; Ezgi Atay; Yi Han Tan; Daniela Wetzel; Ranko Gaćeša; Shijie Zhao; Claudia Mengoni; Shen Jin; Khoa Co; Carsten Peters; Nicola Segata
abstract: Abstract Desulfovibrio spp. are associated with inflammatory diseases and human health, yet limited representative genomes and isolates hinder our understanding of their role in disease. Here, we assembled a comprehensive database of 2658 Desulfovibrio genomes across 90 diseases and 32 countries, including 24 human isolates. Genomic analyses showed extensive species diversity and revealed disease-associated functional traits, including flagellin and adaptation-associated genes (i.e., ureases). Flagellin-mediated Toll-like receptor 5 activation was species-specific and D. desulfuricans flagellin downregulated TGF-beta signalling in murine small intestinal organoids, suggesting impaired immune tolerance. Additionally, we investigated genomic capacity for hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) production, a main Desulfovibrio metabolite. While health- and disease-associated Desulfovibrio spp. mainly encoded dissimilatory sulfate reduction, tetrathionate metabolism-encoding bacteria were exclusively detected in inflammatory bowel diseases, including Proteus mirabilis and Morganella morganii . Overall, our study provides a comprehensive genomic Desulfovibrio resource and identifies new links associating strain variation, functional traits and H 2 S-production with inflammatory diseases.

title: Assessing the potential and cost of enhanced rock weathering in China
authors: Zeyu Wang; Fei Teng; David M. Reiner
abstract: Large-scale carbon dioxide removal is essential for carbon neutrality, but current options face constraints. Enhanced rock weathering is a promising alternative, yet its viability at a national scale in China remains unquantified. Here we show, using a spatially explicit analysis across China’s croplands, that a single-year basalt application could remove 0.44–0.79 billion tonnes of CO2 by 2100, at a net life-cycle-adjusted cost of 127–226 US dollars per tonne of CO2 removed. Particles finer than those typically used commercially provide the most favorable balance between removal potential and cost. Multi-year application has the potential to contribute 5–30% of China’s negative emissions needs by 2060, with priority areas in Northeast, Central-South, and East China. As an initial spatially resolved assessment, this study supports considering enhanced rock weathering in China’s carbon-management portfolio and motivates field trials and coupled soil–river geochemical modeling to constrain weathering, downstream carbon retention, and losses. Enhanced rock weathering contributes 5 to 30 percent of China’s negative emissions needs by 2060 at a net cost of 127 to 226 dollars per tonne of carbon dioxide removed, according to a spatially explicit grid-level analysis of croplands using basalt application scenarios

title: A dual-attribution framework reveals how foreign investment and trade redistribute cobalt availability
authors: Lei Liu; Ling Zhang; Songyan Jiang; Yu Li; Ruishi Li; Zhu Mei; Zengwei Yuan; Jun Chen
abstract: Global resource allocation is increasingly shaped by foreign direct investment (FDI) and international trade, yet their combined effects on distribution of critical mineral availability across countries remain poorly quantified. Here, we develop a dual-attribution framework covering 193 countries and 36 territories that attributes primary cobalt availability according to corporate ownership and secondary availability according to international trade. We compare these estimates with a combined baseline scenario using geographic-production and pre-trade perspectives to assess how ownership and trade reshape country-level cobalt availability. Relative to this baseline, total cobalt availability is higher in 63.6% of countries, while 72.7% show a positive composite change when primary and secondary availability are equally weighted. Although these mechanisms do not alter the global total amount of cobalt available, they reduce its concentration across countries. Our findings highlight how FDI and trade reshape cobalt distribution and support resource-governance policies that account for both host and exporting countries. This study shows how foreign investment and international trade reshape global cobalt availability. A dual-attribution framework reveals higher attributed availability in most countries while reducing country-level concentration.

title: Topological diversity and scintillating dynamics of dipolar surface twists in a van der Waals magnet
authors: Xiaowei Lv; Jiazhuan Qin; Yue Hu; Qingping Wang; Hongyuan Hao; Ke Pei; Senfu Zhang; Xuewen Fu; Han‐Wen Cheng; Zhipeng Hou; Renchao Che
abstract: Realizing diverse configurations and dynamics of skyrmionic solitons offers additional topological and dynamical degrees of freedom for energy-efficient, topology-based spintronic devices. Extending these solitons into three dimensions further amplifies their potential, enabling the selective exploitation of surface- or bulk-topological characteristics, a regime that remains largely unexplored. Here, we report high-density dipolar-interaction-stabilized surface twists atop bulk stripe domains under zero magnetic field, through a systematic investigation of three-dimensional domain architectures in the room-temperature van der Waals ferromagnet Fe3GaTe2. Unlike conventional skyrmions with integer topological charges, these surface twists carry fractional charges and assemble into diverse composite configurations under field swapping, including aggregates of up to 13 surface twists and ring-like structures. Current-driven experiments uncover two distinct dynamic modes: scintillation, marked by the nucleation, annihilation, and helicity switching of surface twists, and ordered motion of bulk skyrmion strings. These behaviors arise from the interplay between spin-transfer torque and local pinning, establishing surface twists as tunable surface-localized topological states whose dynamics are decoupled from their bulk counterparts, thereby enabling versatile hybrid spintronic functionalities. Authors investigate the field- and current-driven dynamics of three-dimensional magnetic textures in Fe3GaTe2, revealing topological diversity and distinct dynamical behaviors at the surface and in the bulk.

title: The influence of vapor pressure deficit changes on global terrestrial evapotranspiration
authors: Yuxin Miao; Guofeng Zhu; Yuhao Wang; Enwei Huang; Qingyang Wang; Yani Gun; Zhijie Zheng; Jiangwei Yang; Wenmin Li; Ziwen Liu
abstract: Abstract. Vapor pressure deficit (VPD) is increasingly recognized as the primary driver of uncertainty in future global evapotranspiration (E) trends. Accurately characterizing the spatiotemporal dynamics of VPD and clarifying its mechanisms of influence on terrestrial E are crucial for improving water-use efficiency, optimizing ecosystem structure and function, and addressing the challenges of global climate change. Previous studies, however, have largely concentrated on the physiological regulation of vegetation transpiration (Et) at the micro scale. Here, we integrate multi-source remote sensing products and reanalysis datasets spanning 1981–2020 to quantitatively disentangle the contributions of VPD to E and assess its role in shaping global terrestrial evapotranspiration. Our results demonstrate that: (1) across 60.7 % of the global land surface, E increased with rising VPD, while in arid regions with limited soil moisture the effect was generally weak; (2) VPD regulates E primarily by modulating Et, with elevated VPD directly enhancing transpiration; (3) the regulation of E by VPD exhibits a clear climatic gradient: arid zones (1.31 kPa) > humid zones (0.32 kPa), and the tropical (0.79 kPa) > temperate (0.68 kPa) > cold (0.28 kPa) > polar (0.07 kPa). By elucidating the dominant pathways and regional heterogeneity of VPD–E interactions at the global scale, this study strengthens the mechanistic understanding of the coupled warming–atmospheric aridity–water flux system. These findings provide quantitative constraints for predicting terrestrial water-cycle changes under global warming and offer scientific evidence to support targeted climate adaptation strategies worldwide.

title: The influence of lakes and reservoirs on estimated flood peaks at hourly vs. daily timescale in the Alps
authors: Jonas Götte; Paul C. Astagneau; Manuela I. Brunner
abstract: Abstract. Water bodies such as lakes and reservoirs can play a crucial role in reducing flood peaks both on daily and hourly timescales. While the effect of water bodies on flood peaks at different time resolutions has been demonstrated in the past, it remains unclear how they affect the ratio between daily and hourly peaks. Here, we analyse how water bodies attenuate flood peaks at daily and hourly time resolution and the relationship between flood peaks at these two time scales using two approaches: (1) four local case studies with gauges upstream and downstream of reservoirs, and (2) a large-sample hydrological dataset covering Switzerland. Our results show that hourly flows are dampened much more strongly than daily flows, which leads to similar daily and hourly flood peaks downstream of reservoirs. Specifically, our case study analysis highlights that (sub-)hourly flows are attenuated by up to 70 percent downstream of reservoirs during flood events with a 10-year return period. We also find that the attenuation effect is particularly pronounced in catchments that are heavily influenced by water bodies, i.e. those catchments where more than 60 percent of the area contributes to water body inflow. We conclude that considering water body influence on flood peaks is crucial to understand the similarity between daily and hourly flood peaks and that it should be considered in large-sample analyses using suitable metrics.

title: Resistance indicators in sewage microbiota mirror clinical antibiotic use with temporal lag linked to host
authors: Connor Brown; MA. Rumi; Lauren F. McDaniel; Ayella Maile-Moskowitz; Justin Sein; L. Nguyen; M. Choi; Fadi Hindi; James I Mullet; M. Emon; Nazifa Ahmed Moumi; M. F. Blair; B. C. Davis; J. Rao; Anthony W. Baffoe-Bonnie
abstract: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) offers a promising window into community pathogens but extending it to antibiotic resistance (AR) is complicated by ecological and physical processes within sewer systems. The epidemiological meaning of antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) abundances in sewage remains unclear because signals reflect both human-derived inputs and in-sewer microbial dynamics. Using a unique 5-year dataset of outpatient antibiotic prescriptions and a yearlong, twice-weekly metagenomic survey of a single wastewater treatment plant, we differentiate associations between sewage-borne antibiotic-resistant bacteria and community antibiotic use. We find that ARGs linked to Enterobacteriaceae track closely with antibiotic usage, while those associated with ecologically-distinct Pseudomonadaceae show lagged correlations of 1–3 months. Nested statistical modeling further links Pseudomonas MAG dynamics with lagged sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim use after accounting for sewage characteristics and seasonality. Our results demonstrate that WBS can capture local patterns of epidemiologically relevant AR when microbial ecological factors shaping sewage signals are considered. Profiles of antibiotic resistance genes in wastewater still often lack epidemiological context. In this study, the authors use wastewater metagenomics and antibiotic use data to reveal a variable lagging association between human antibiotic consumption and antibiotic resistance genes in sewage-derived bacterial hosts.

title: Precious metal free tunable manganese oxides for sustainable anion exchange membrane fuel cells
authors: Xuepeng Zhong; Chuangxin Ge; Shengjie Zhang; Hainan Wei; Menghao Yang; Xiong Zhang; Jiuyi Wang; Yang Zhao; Jiayi Li; Na Xu; Lijun Sui; Toshinari Koketsu; Chenlong Gao; Lin Zhuang; Nicolás Alonso‐Vante
abstract: Abstract Eliminating platinum group metals from cathode catalysts in low-temperature polymer electrolyte fuel cells is highly important for addressing the sustainability challenge fuel cell systems face. Here, we propose modifying the electronic structure of Li-intercalated layered Mn-oxide as a cathode catalyst to overcome the activity/stability tradeoff in anion exchange membrane fuel cells. To achieve this goal, we deploy a precious metal free catalyst design strategy involving atomically dispersed p -block metal Sn doped in Li 2 MnO 3 , in addition to d -block metals, which has been poorly explored in the research thus far. Operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy and rapid freeze-quench 119 Sn Mössbauer methodology are employed to visualize the catalytic dynamics, revealing that part of Mn 4+ ions are converted into Mn 3+ ions, whereas Sn 4+ ions remain unchanged during the oxygen reduction reaction. Under H 2 /O 2 conditions, anion exchange membrane fuel cells employing Li 2 Mn 0.9 Sn 0.1 O 3 cathodes achieve peak power densities above 1.0 W cm -2 geo and 3.96 W mg -1 Pt . This work demonstrates the beneficial modulation of the electronic structure through p -block metal substitution in earth-abundant Mn-enriched oxide materials.

title: Pipeline infrastructure for hydrogen transport in the United States
authors: Ayush Singh; Haibo Zhai; Yevhen I. Holubnyak; Curtis Biggs
abstract: Pipeline infrastructure is crucial for regional hydrogen transport. However, existing pipeline models have remarkably underestimated the construction-related material and labor costs compared to U.S. historical data. To cope with this problem and establish sustainable infrastructure, we develop integrated performance, economic and life cycle emissions models to comparatively evaluate dedicated pipelines and repurposed natural gas pipelines for hydrogen transport across the country. We find that the levelized cost of hydrogen transport via dedicated pipelines varies with numerous factors, such as location, capacity, and distance; there are similar variabilities in the cost of hydrogen transport via repurposed natural gas pipelines; and although leveraging existing natural gas pipelines can substantially reduce upfront capital expenditures, it may involve tradeoffs in cost and life cycle emissions. Here, we show that the integrated pipeline models and multi-criteria analysis can better guide engineering design, planning, and investment decisions on building nationwide hydrogen transport networks. This study compares new and repurposed gas pipelines for nationwide hydrogen transport, showing how costs and life-cycle emissions vary across options and highlighting trade-offs for infrastructure planning and investment.
